text: As the letter A is the first of all letters, so the eternal God is first in the world
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What Profit have those derived from learning, who worship not the good feet of Him who is possessed of pure knowledge?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They who are united to the glorious feet of Him who passes swiftly over the flower of the mind, shall flourish long above all worlds
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To those who meditate the feet of Him who is void of desire or aversion, evil shall never come
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The two-fold deeds that spring from darkness shall not adhere to those who delight in the true praise of God
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those shall long proposer who abide in the faultless way of Him who has destroyed the five desires of the senses
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Anxiety of mind cannot be removed, except from those who are united to the feet of Him who is incomparable
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: None can swim the sea of vice, but those who are united to the feet of that gracious Being who is a sea of virtue
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The head that worships not the feet of Him who is possessed of eight attributes, is as useless as a sense without the power of sensation
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: None can swim the great sea of births but those who are united to the feet of God
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: By the continuance of rain the world is preserved in existence; it is therefore worthy to be called ambrosia
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Rain produces good food, and is itself food
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the cloud, withholding rain, deceive (our hopes) hunger will long distress the sea-girt spacious world
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the abundance of wealth imparting rain diminish, the labour of the plough must cease
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Rain by its absence ruins men; and by its existence restores them to fortune
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If no drop falls from the clouds, not even the green blade of grass will be seen
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even the wealth of the wide sea will be diminished, if the cloud that has drawn (its waters) up gives them not back again (in rain)
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the heaven dry up, neither yearly festivals, nor daily worship will be offered in this world, to the celestials
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If rain fall not, penance and alms-deeds will not dwell within this spacious world
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If it be said that the duties of life cannot be discharged by any person without water, so without rain there cannot be the flowing of water
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The end and aim of all treatise is to extol beyond all other excellence, the greatness of those who, while abiding in the rule of conduct peculiar to their state, have abandoned all desire
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To describe the measure of the greatness of those who have forsaken the two-fold desires, is like counting the dead
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The greatness of those who have discovered the properties of both states of being, and renounced the world, shines forth on earth (beyond all others)
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who guides his five senses by the hook of wisdom will be a seed in the world of heaven
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Indra, the king of the inhabitants of the spacious heaven, is himself, a sufficient proof of the strength of him who has subdued his five senses
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The great will do those things which is difficult to be done; but the mean cannot do them
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The world is within the knowledge of him who knows the properties of taste, sight, touch, hearing and smell
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The hidden words of the men whose words are full of effect, will shew their greatness to the world
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The anger of those who have ascended the mountain of goodness, though it continue but for a moment, cannot be resisted
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The virtuous are truly called Anthanar; because in their conduct towards all creatures they are clothed in kindness
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Virtue will confer heaven and wealth; what greater source of happiness can man possess ?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There can be no greater source of good than (the practice of) virtue; there can be no greater source of evil than the forgetfulness of it
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As much as possible, in every way, incessantly practise virtue
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let him who does virtuous deeds be of spotless mind; to that extent is virtue; all else is vain show
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That conduct is virtue which is free from these four things, viz, malice, desire, anger and bitter speech
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Defer not virtue to another day; receive her now; and at the dying hour she will be your undying friend
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The fruit of virtue need not be described in books; it may be inferred from seeing the bearer of a palanquin and the rider therein
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If one allows no day to pass without some good being done, his conduct will be a stone to block up the passage to other births
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Only that pleasure which flows from domestic virtue is pleasure; all else is not pleasure, and it is without praise
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That is virtue which each ought to do, and that is vice which each should shun
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He will be called a (true) householder, who is a firm support to the virtuous of the three orders in
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He will be said to flourish in domestic virtue who aids the forsaken, the poor, and the dead
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The chief (duty of the householder) is to preserve the five-fold rule (of conduct) towards the manes, the Gods, his guests, his relations and himself
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: His descendants shall never fail who, living in the domestic state, fears vice (in the acquisition of property) and shares his food (with others)
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the married life possess love and virtue, these will be both its duty and reward
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What will he who lives virtuously in the domestic state gain by going into the other, (ascetic) state ?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Among all those who labour (for future happiness) he is greatest who lives well in the household state
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The householder who, not swerving from virtue, helps the ascetic in his way, endures more than those who endure penance
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The marriage state is truly called virtue The other state is also good, if others do not reproach it
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who on earth has lived in the conjugal state as he should live, will be placed among the Gods who dwell in heaven
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: She who has the excellence of home virtues, and can expend within the means of her husband, is a help in the domestic state
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the wife be devoid of domestic excellence, whatever (other) greatness be possessed, the conjugal state, is nothing
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If his wife be eminent (in virtue), what does (that man) not possess ? If she be without excellence, what does (he) possess ?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What is more excellent than a wife, if she possess the stability of chastity ?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If she, who does not worship God, but who rising worships her husband, say, "let it rain," it will rain
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: She is a wife who unweariedly guards herself, takes care of her husband, and preserves an unsullied fame
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What avails the guard of a prison ? The chief guard of a woman is her chastity
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If women shew reverence to their husbands, they will obtain great excellence in the world where the gods flourish
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The man whose wife seeks not the praise (of chastity) cannot walk with lion-like stately step, before those who revile them
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The excellence of a wife is the good of her husband; and good children are the jewels of that goodness
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Among all the benefits that may be acquired, we know no greater benefit than the acquisition of intelligent children
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The evils of the seven births shall not touch those who abtain children of a good disposition, free from vice
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Men will call their sons their wealth, because it flows to them through the deeds which they (sons) perform on their behalf
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The rice in which the little hand of their children has dabbled will be far sweeter (to the parent) than ambrosia
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The touch of children gives pleasure to the body, and the hearing of their words, pleasure to the ear
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: "The pipe is sweet, the lute is sweet," say those who have not heard the prattle of their own children
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The benefit which a father should confer on his son is to give him precedence in the assembly of the learned
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That their children should possess knowledge is more pleasing to all men of this great earth than to themselves
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The mother who hears her son called "a wise man" will rejoice more than she did at his birth
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (So to act) that it may be said "by what great penance did his father beget him," is the benefit which a son should render to his father
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is there any fastening that can shut in love ? Tears of the affectionate will publish the love that is within
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who are destitute of love appropriate all they have to themselves; but those who possess love consider even their bones to belong to others
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They say that the union of soul and body in man is the fruit of the union of love and virtue (in a former birth)
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Love begets desire: and that (desire) begets the immeasureable excellence of friendship
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: These are the fruits of tranquil life of love
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The ignorant say that love is an ally to virtue only, but it is also a help to get out of vice
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Virtue will burn up the soul which is without love, even as the sun burns up the creature which is without bone, ie worms
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The domestic state of that man whose mind is without love is like the flourishing of a withered tree upon the parched desert
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Of what avail are all the external members (of the body) to those who are destitute of love, the internal member
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That body alone which is inspired with love contains a living soul: if void of it, (the body) is bone overlaid with skin
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The whole design of living in the domestic state and laying up (property) is (to be able) to exercise the benevolence of hospitality
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is not fit that one should wish his guests to be outside (his house) even though he were eating the food of immortality
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The domestic life of the man that daily entertains the guests who come to him shall not be laid waste by poverty
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Lakshmi with joyous mind shall dwell in the house of that man who, with cheerful countenance, entertains the good as guests
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is it necessary to sow the field of the man who, having feasted his guests, eats what may remain ?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who, having entertained the guests that have come, looks out for others who may yet come, will be a welcome guest to the inhabitants of heaven
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The advantages of benevolence cannot be measured; the measure (of the virtue) of the guests (entertained) is the only measure
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who have taken no part in the benevolence of hospitality shall (at length lament) saying, "we have laboured and laid up wealth and are now without support."
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That stupidity which excercises no hospitality is poverty in the midst of wealth It is the property of the stupid
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As the Anicham flower fades in smelling, so fades the guest when the face is turned away
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sweet words are those which imbued with love and free from deceit flow from the mouth of the virtuous
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sweet speech, with a cheerful countenance is better than a gift made with a joyous mind
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sweet speech, flowing from the heart (uttered) with a cheerful countenance and a sweet look, is true virtue
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sorrow-increasing poverty shall not come upon those who use towards all, pleasure-increasing sweetness of speech
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Humility and sweetness of speech are the ornaments of man; all others are not (ornaments)
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a man, while seeking to speak usefully, speaks also sweetly, his sins will diminish and his virtue increase
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That speech which, while imparting benefits ceases not to please, will yield righteousness (for this world) and merit (for the next world)
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sweet speech, free from harm to others, will give pleasure both in this world and in the next
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Why does he use harsh words, who sees the pleasure which sweet speech yields ?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To say disagreeable things when agreeable are at hand is like eating unripe fruit when there is ripe
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The gift of) heaven and earth is not an equivalent for a benefit which is conferred where none had been received
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A favour conferred in the time of need, though it be small (in itself), is (in value) much larger than the world
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If we weigh the excellence of a benefit which is conferred without weighing the return, it is larger than the sea
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though the benefit conferred be as small as a millet seed, those who know its advantage will consider it as large as a palmyra fruit
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The benefit itself is not the measure of the benefit; the worth of those who have received it is its measure
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Forsake not the friendship of those who have been your staff in adversity Forget not be benevolence of the blameless
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The wise) will remember throughout their seven-fold births the love of those who have wiped away their affliction
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is not good to forget a benefit; it is good to forget an injury even in the very moment (in which it is inflicted)
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though one inflict an injury great as murder, it will perish before the thought of one benefit (formerly) conferred
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who has killed every virtue may yet escape; there is no escape for him who has killed a benefit
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That equity which consists in acting with equal regard to each of (the three) divisions of men [enemies, strangers and friends] is a pre-eminent virtue
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth of the man of rectitude will not perish, but will bring happiness also to his posterity
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Forsake in the very moment (of acquisition) that gain which, though it should bring advantage, is without equity
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The worthy and unworthy may be known by the existence or otherwise of good offsprings
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Loss and gain come not without cause; it is the ornament of the wise to preserve evenness of mind (under both)
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let him whose mind departing from equity commits sin well consider thus within himself, "I shall perish."
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The great will not regard as poverty the low estate of that man who dwells in the virtue of equity
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To incline to neither side, but to rest impartial as the even-fixed scale is the ornament of the wise
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Freedom from obliquity of speech is rectitude, if there be (corresponding) freedom from bias of mind
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The true merchandize of merchants is to guard and do by the things of others as they do by their own
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Self-control will place (a man) among the Gods; the want of it will drive (him) into the thickest darkness (of hell)
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let self-control be guarded as a treasure; there is no greater source of good for man than that
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Knowing that self-control is knowledge, if a man should control himself, in the prescribed course, such self-control will bring him distinction among the wise
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: More lofty than a mountain will be the greatness of that man who without swerving from his domestic state, controls himself
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Humility is good in all; but especially in the rich it is (the excellence of) higher riches
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Should one throughout a single birth, like a tortoise keep in his five senses, the fruit of it will prove a safe-guard to him throughout the seven-fold births.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Whatever besides you leave unguarded, guard your tongue; otherwise errors of speech and the consequent misery will ensue
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a man's speech be productive of a single evil, all the good by him will be turned into evil
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wound which has been burnt in by fire may heal, but a wound burnt in by the tongue will never heal
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Virtue, seeking for an opportunity, will come into the path of that man who, possessed of learning and self-control, guards himself against anger
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Propriety of conduct leads to eminence, it should therefore be preserved more carefully than life
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let propriety of conduct be laboriously preserved and guarded; though one know and practise and excel in many virtues, that will be an eminent aid
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Propriety of conduct is true greatness of birth, and impropriety will sink into a mean birth
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A Brahman though he should forget the Vedas may recover it by reading; but, if he fail in propriety of conduct even his high birth will be destroyed
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Just as the envious man will be without wealth, so will the man of destitute of propriety of conduct be without greatness
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those firm in mind will not slacken in their observance of the proprieties of life, knowing, as they do, the misery that flows from the transgression from them
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: From propriety of conduct men obtain greatness; from impropriety comes insufferable disgrace
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Propriety of conduct is the seed of virtue; impropriety will ever cause sorrow
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who study propriety of conduct will not speak evil, even forgetfully
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who know not how to act agreeably to the world, though they have learnt many things, are still ignorant
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The folly of desiring her who is the property of another will not be found in those who know (the attributes of) virtue and (the rights of) property
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Among all those who stand on the outside of virtue, there are no greater fools than those who stand outside their neighbour's door
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Certainly they are no better than dead men who desire evil towards the wife of those who undoubtingly confide in them
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: However great one may be, what does it avail if, without at all considering his guilt, he goes unto the wife of another ?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who thinks lightly of going into the wife of another acquires guilt that will abide with him imperishably and for ever
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Hatred, sin, fear, disgrace; these four will never leave him who goes in to his neighbour's wife
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who desires not the womanhood of her who should walk according to the will of another will be praised as a virtuous house-holder
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That noble manliness which looks not at the wife of another is the virtue and dignity of the great
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is it asked, "who are those who shall obtain good in this world surrounded by the terror-producing sea ?" Those who touch not the shoulder of her who belongs to another.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though a man perform no virtuous deeds and commit (every) vice, it will be well if he desire not the womanhood of her who is within the limit (of the house) of another.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To bear with those who revile us, just as the earth bears up those who dig it, is the first of virtues.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Bear with reproach even when you can retaliate; but to forget it will be still better than that.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To neglect hospitality is poverty of poverty. To bear with the ignorant is might of might.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If you desire that greatness should never leave, you preserve in your conduct the exercise of patience
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The wise) will not at all esteem the resentful. They will esteem the patient just as the gold which they lay up with care.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The pleasure of the resentful continues for a day. The praise of the patient will continue until (the final destruction of) the world.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though others inflict injuries on you, yet compassionating the evil (that will come upon them) it will be well not to do them anything contrary to virtue.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a man by patience overcome those who through pride commit excesses.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who bear with the uncourteous speech of the insolent are as pure as the ascetics.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who endure abstinence from food are great, next to those who endure the uncourteous speech of others.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a man esteem that disposition which is free from envy in the same manner as propriety of conduct.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Amongst all attainable excellences there is none equal to that of being free from envy towords others
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Of him who instead of rejoicing in the wealth of others, envies it, it will be said "he neither desires virtue not wealth".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The wise) knowing the misery that comes from transgression will not through envy commit unrighteous deeds.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To those who cherish envy that is enough. Though free from enemies that (envy) will bring destruction.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who is envious at a gift (made to another) will with his relations utterly perish destitute of food and rainment.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Lakshmi envying (the prosperity) of the envious man will depart and introduce him to her sister.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Envy will destroy (a man's) wealth (in his world) and drive him into the pit of fire (in the world to come).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth of a man of envious mind and the poverty of the righteous will be pondered.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Never have the envious become great; never have those who are free from envy been without greatness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a man departing from equity covet the property (of others), at that very time will his family be destroyed and guilt be incurred.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who blush at the want of equity will not commit disgraceful acts through desire of the profit that may be gained.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who desire the higher pleasures (of heaven) will not act unjustly through desire of the trifling joy. (in this life).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wise who have conquered their senses and are free from crime, will not covet (the things of others), with the thought "we are destitute".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What is the advantage of extensive and accurate knowledge if a man through covetousness act senselessly towards all ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If he, who through desire of the virtue of kindness abides in the domestic state i.e., the path in which it may be obtained, covet (the property of others) and think of evil methods (to obtain it), he will perish.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Desire not the gain of covetousness. In the enjoyment of its fruits there is no glory.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If it is weighed, "what is the indestructibility of wealth," it is freedom from covetousness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Lakshmi, knowing the manner (in which she may approach) will immediately come to those wise men who, knowing that it is virtue, covet not the property of others.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To covet (the wealth of another) regardless of consequences will bring destruction. That greatness (of mind) which covets not will give victory.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though one do not even speak of virtue and live in sin, it will be well if it be said of him "he does not backbite".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To smile deceitfully (in another's presence) after having reviled him to his destruction (behind his back) is a greater evil than the commission of (every other) sin and the destruction of (every) virtue.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Death rather than life will confer upon the deceitful backbiter the profit which (the treatises on) virtue point out.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though you speak without kindness before another's face speak not in his absence words which regard not the evil subsequently resulting from it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The emptiness of that man's mind who (merely) praises virtue will be seen from the meanness of reviling another behind his back.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The character of the faults of that man who publishes abroad the faults of others will be sought out and published
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who know not to live in friendship with amusing conversation will by back-biting estrange even their relatives.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What will those not do to strangers whose nature leads them to publish abroad the faults of their intimate friends ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The world through charity supports the weight of those who reproach others observing their absence.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If they observed their own faults as they observe the faults of others, would any evil happen to men ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who to the disgust of many speaks useless things will be despised by all.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To speak useless things in the presence of many is a greater evil than to do unkind things towards friends.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That conversation in which a man utters forth useless things will say of him "he is without virtue".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The words devoid of profit or pleasure which a man speaks will, being inconsistent with virtue, remove him from goodness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the good speak vain words their eminence and excellence will leave them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Call not him a man who parades forth his empty words. Call him the chaff of men.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let the wise if they will, speak things without excellence; it will be well for them not to speak useless things.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wise who seek after rare pleasures will not speak words that have not much weight in them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those wise men who are without faults and are freed from ignorance will not even forgetfully speak things that profit not.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Speak what is useful, and speak not useless words.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who have experience of evil deeds will not fear, but the excellent will fear the pride of sin.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Because evil produces evil, therefore should evil be feared more than fire.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To do no evil to enemies will be called the chief of all virtues.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even though forgetfulness meditate not the ruin of another. Virtue will meditate the ruin of him who thus meditates.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Commit not evil, saying, "I am poor": if you do, you will become poorer still.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let him not do evil to others who desires not that sorrows should pursue him
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: However great be the enmity men have incurred they may still live. The enmity of sin will incessantly pursue and kill.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Destruction will dwell at the heels of those who commit evil even as their shadow that leaves them not.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a man love himself, let him not commit any sin however small.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Know ye that he is freed from destruction who commits no evil, going to neither side of the right path.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Benevolence seeks not a return. What does the world give back to the clouds ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: All the wealth acquired with perseverance by the worthy is for the exercise of benevolence.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is difficult to obtain another good equal to benevolence either in this world or in that of the gods.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He truly lives who knows (and discharges) the proper duties (of benevolence). He who knows them not will be reckoned among the dead.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth of that man of eminent knowledge who desires to exercise the benevolence approved of by the world, is like the full waters of a city-tank.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth of a man (possessed of the virtue) of benevolence is like the ripening of a fruitful tree in the midst of a town.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If wealth be in the possession of a man who has the great excellence (of benevolence), it is like a tree which as a medicine is an infallible cure for disease.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wise who know what is duty will not scant their benevolence even when they are without wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The poverty of a benevolent man, is nothing but his inability to exercise the same.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If it be said that loss will result from benevolence, such loss is worth being procured even by the sale of one's self.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To give to the destitute is true charity. All other gifts have the nature of (what is done for) a measured return.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To beg is evil, even though it were said that it is a good path (to heaven). To give is good, even though it were said that those who do so cannot obtain heaven.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (Even in a low state) not to adopt the mean expedient of saying "I have nothing," but to give, is the characteristic of the mad of noble birth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To see men begging from us in disagreeable, until we see their pleasant countenance.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The power of those who perform penance is the power of enduring hunger. It is inferior to the power of those who remove the hunger (of others).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The removal of the killing hunger of the poor is the place for one to lay up his wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The fiery disease of hunger shall never touch him who habitually distributes his food to others.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Do the hard-eyed who lay up and lose their possessions not know the happiness which springs from the pleasure of giving ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Solitary and unshared eating for the sake of filling up one's own riches is certainly much more unpleasant than begging.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Nothing is more unpleasant than death: yet even that is pleasant where charity cannot be exercised.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Give to the poor and live with praise. There is no greater profit to man than that.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Whatsoever is spoken in the world will abide as praise upon that man who gives alms to the poor.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is nothing that stands forth in the world imperishable, except fame, exalted in solitary greatness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If one has acquired extensive fame within the limits of this earth, the world of the Gods will no longer praise those sages who have attained that world.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Prosperity to the body of fame, resulting in poverty to the body of flesh and the stability to the former arising from the death of the latter, are achievable only by the wise.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If you are born (in this world), be born with qualities conductive to fame. From those who are destitute of them it will be better not to be born.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Why do those who cannot live with praise, grieve those who despise them, instead of grieving themselves for their own inability.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not to beget fame will be esteemed a disgrace by the wise in this world.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The ground which supports a body without fame will diminish in its rich produce.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those live who live without disgrace. Those who live without fame live not.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth of kindness is wealth of wealth, in as much as the wealth of property is possessed by the basest of men.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (Stand) in the good path, consider, and be kind. Even considering according to the conflicting tenets of the different sects, kindness will be your best aid, (in the acquisition of heavenly bliss).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They will never enter the world of darkness and wretchedness whose minds are the abode of kindness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The wise) say that the evils, which his soul would dread, will never come upon the man who exercises kindness and protects the life (of other creatures).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: This great rich earth over which the wind blows, is a witness that sorrow never comes upon the kind-hearted.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The wise) say that those who neglect kindness and practise cruelties, neglected virtue (in their former birth), and forgot (the sorrows which they must suffer).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As this world is not for those who are without wealth, so that world is not for those who are without kindness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who are without wealth may, at some future time, become prosperous; those who are destitute of kindness are utterly destitute; for them there is no change.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If you consider, the virtue of him who is without kindness is like the perception of the true being by him who is without wisdom.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When a man is about to rush upon those who are weaker than himself, let him remember how he has stood (trembling) before those who are stronger than himself.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: How can he be possessed of kindness, who to increase his own flesh, eats the flesh of other creatures.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As those possess no property who do not take care of it, so those possess no kindness who feed on flesh.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Like the (murderous) mind of him who carries a weapon (in his hand), the mind of him who feasts with pleasure on the body of another (creature), has no regard for goodness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If it be asked what is kindness and what its opposite, the answer would be preservation and destruction of life; and therefore it is not right to feed on the flesh (obtained by taking away life).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not to eat flesh contributes to the continuance of life; therefore if a man eat flesh, hell will not open its mouth (to let him escape out, after he has once fallen in).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the world does not destroy life for the purpose of eating, then no one would sell flesh for the sake of money.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If men should come to know that flesh is nothing but the unclean ulcer of a body, let them abstain from eating it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wise, who have freed themselves from mental delusion, will not eat the flesh which has been severed from an animal.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not to kill and eat (the flesh of) an animal, is better than the pouring forth of ghee etc., in a thousand sacrifices.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: All creatures will join their hands together, and worship him who has never taken away life, nor eaten flesh.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The nature of religious discipline consists, in the endurance (by the ascetic) of the sufferings which it brings on himself, and in abstaining from giving pain to others.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Austerities can only be borne, and their benefits enjoyed, by those who have practised them (in a former birth); it will be useless for those who have not done so, to attempt to practise them (now).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is to provide food etc, for the ascetics who have abandoned (the desire of earthly possessions) that other persons have forgotten (to practise) austerity ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If (the ascetic) desire the destruction of his enemies, or the aggrandizement of his friends, it will be effected by (the power of) his austerities.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Religious dislipline is practised in this world, because it secures the attainment of whatever one may wish to enjoy (in the world to come).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those discharge their duty who perform austerities; all others accomplish their own destruction, through the entanglement of the desire (of riches and sensual pleasure).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Just as gold is purified as heated in the fire, will those shine, who have endured the burning of pain (in frequent austerities).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: All other creatures will worship him who has attained the control of his own soul.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who have attained the power which religious discipline confers, will be able also to pass the limit of Yama, (the God of death).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Because there are few who practise austerity and many who do not, there are many destitute and few rich in this world.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The five elements (of his body) will laugh within him at the feigned conduct of the deceitful minded man.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What avails an appearance (of sanctity) high as heaven, if his mind suffers (the indulgence) of conscious sin.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The assumed appearance of power, by a man who has no power (to restrain his senses and perform austerity), is like a cow feeding on grass covered with a tiger's skin.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who hides himself under the mask of an ascetic and commits sins, like a sportsman who conceals himself in the thicket to catch birds.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The false conduct of those who say they have renounced all desire will one day bring them sorrows that will make them cry out, "Oh! what have we done, what have we done".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Amongst living men there are none so hard-hearted as those who without to saking (desire) in their heart, falsely take the appearance of those who have forsaken (it).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The world) contains persons whose outside appears (as fair) as the (red) berry of the Abrus, but whose inside is as black as the nose of that berry.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There are many men of masked conduct, who perform their ablutions, and (make a show) of greatness, while their mind is defiled (with guilt).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As, in its use, the arrow is crooked, and the curved lute is straight, so by their deeds, (and not by their appearance) let (the uprightness or crookedness of) men be estimated.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is no need of a shaven crown, nor of tangled hair, if a man abstain from those deeds which the wise have condemned.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let him, who desires not to be despised, keep his mind from (the desire of) defrauding another of the smallest thing.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even the thought (of sin) is sin; think not then of crafiily stealing the property of another.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The property, which is acquired by fraud, will entirely perish, even while it seems to increase.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The eager desire of defrauding others will, when it brings forth its fruit, produce undying sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The study of kindness and the exercise of benevolence is not with those who watch for another's forgetfulness, though desire of his property.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They cannot walk steadfastly, according to rule, who eagerly desire to defraud others.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That black-knowledge which is called fraud, is not in those who desire that greatness which is called rectitude.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Deceit dwells in the mind of those who are conversant with fraud, even as virtue in the minds of those who are conversant with rectitude.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those, who are acquainted with nothing but fraud, will perish in the very commission of transgression.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even their body will fail the fraudulent; but even the world of the gods will not fail those who are free from fraud.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Truth is the speaking of such words as are free from the least degree of evil (to others).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even falsehood has the nature of truth, if it confer a benefit that is free from fault.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let not a man knowingly tell a lie; for after he has told the lie, his mind will burn him (with the memory of his guilt).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who, in his conduct, preserves a mind free from deceit, will dwell in the minds of all men.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He, who speaks truth with all his heart, is superior to those who make gifts and practise austerities.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is no praise like the praise of never uttering a falsehood: without causing any suffering, it will lead to every virtue.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a man has the power to abstain from falsehood, it will be well with him, even though he practise no other virtue.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Purity of body is produced by water and purity of mind by truthfulness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: All lamps of nature are not lamps; the lamp of truth is the lamp of the wise.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Amidst all that we have seen (described) as real (excellence), there is nothing so good as truthfulness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He restrains his anger who restrains it when it can injure; when it cannot injure, what does it matter whether he restrain it, or not ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Anger is bad, even when it cannot injure; when it can injure; there is no greater evil.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Forget anger towards every one, as fountains of evil spring from it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is there a greater enemy than anger, which kills both laughter and joy ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
