work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a man would guard himself, let him guard against anger; if he do not guard it, anger will kill him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The fire of anger will burn up even the pleasant raft of friendship.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Destruction will come upon him who ragards anger as a good thing, as surely as the hand of him who strikes the ground will not fail.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though one commit things against you as painful (to bear) as if a bundle of fire had been thrust upon you, it will be well, to refrain, if possible, from anger.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a man never indulges anger in his heart, he will at once obtain whatever he has thought of.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those, who give way to excessive anger, are no better than dead men; but those, who are freed from it, are equal to those who are freed (from death).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is the determination of the spotless not to cause sorrow to others, although they could (by so causing) obtain the wealth which confers greatness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is the determination of the spotless not to do evil, even in return, to those who have cherished enmity and done them evil.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In an ascetic inflict suffering even on those who hate him, when he has not done them any evil, it will afterwards give him irretrievable sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The (proper) punishment to those who have done evil (to you), is to put them to shame by showing them kindness, in return and to forget both the evil and the good done on both sides.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What benefit has he derived from his knowledge, who does not endeavour to keep off pain from another as much as from himself ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let not a man consent to do those things to another which, he knows, will cause sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is the chief of all virtues not knowingly to do any person evil, even in the lowest degree, and at any time
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Why does a man inflict upon other creatures those sufferings, which he has found by experience are sufferings to himself ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a man inflict sorrow upon others in the morning, it will come upon him unsought in the very evening.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sorrow will come upon those who cause pain to others; therfore those, who desire to be free from sorrow, give no pain to others.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Never to destroy life is the sum of all virtuous conduct. The destruction of life leads to every evil.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The chief of all (the virtues) which authors have summed up, is the partaking of food that has been shared with others, and the preservation of the mainfold life of other creatures.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not to destroy life is an incomparably (great) good next to it in goodness ranks freedom from falsehood.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Good path is that which considers how it may avoid killing any creature.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Of all those who, fearing the permanence of earthly births, have abandoned desire, he is the chief who, fearing (the guilt of) murder, considers how he may avoid the destruction of life.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Yama, the destroyer of life, will not attack the life of him, who acts under the determination of never destroying life.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let no one do that which would destroy the life of another, although he should by so doing, lose his own life.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The advantage which might flow from destroying life in sacrifice, is dishonourable to the wise (who renounced the world), even although it should be said to be productive of great good.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Men who destroy life are base men, in the estimation of those who know the nature of meanness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The wise) will say that men of diseased bodies, who live in degradation and in poverty, are those who separated the life from the body of animals (in a former birth).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That ignorance which considers those things to be stable which are not so, is dishonourable (to the wise).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The acquisition of wealth is like the gathering together of an assembly for a theatre; its expenditure is like the breaking up of that assembly.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Wealth is perishable; let those who obtain it immediately practise those (virtues) which are imperishable.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Time, which shows itself (to the ignorant) as if it were something (real) is in the estimation of the wise (only) a saw which cuts down life.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let virtuous deeds be done quickly, before the biccup comes making the tongue silent.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: This world possesses the greatness that one who yesterday was is not today.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Innumerable are the thoughts which occupy the mind of (the unwise), who know not that they shall live another moment.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The love of the soul to the body is like (the love of) a bird to its egg which it flies away from and leaves empty.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Death is like sleep; birth is like awaking from it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It seems as if the soul, which takes a temporary shelter in a body, had not attained a home.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Whatever thing, a man has renounced, by that thing; he cannot suffer pain.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: After a man has renounced (all things), there will still be many things in this world (which he may enjoy); if he should desire them, let him, while it is time abandon. (the world).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let the five senses be destroyed; and at the same time, let everything be abandoned that (the ascetic) has (formerly) desired.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To be altogether destitute is the proper condition of those who perform austerities; if they possess anything, it will change (their resolution) and bring them back to their confused state.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What means the addition of other things those who are attempting to cut off (future) births, when even their body is too much (for them).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who destroys the pride which says "I", "mine" will enter a world which is difficult even to the Gods to attain.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sorrows will never let go their hold of those who give not up their hold of desire.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who have entirely renounced (all things and all desire) have obtained (absorption into God); all others wander in confusion, entangled in the net of (many) births.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: At the moment in which desire has been abandoned, (other) births will be cut off; when that has not been done, instability will be seen.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Desire the desire of Him who is without desire; in order to renounce desire, desire that desire.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Inglorious births are produced by the confusion (of mind) which considers those things to be real which are not real.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A clear, undimmed vision of things will deliver its possessors from the darkness of future births, and confer the felicity (of heaven).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Heaven is nearer than earth to those men of purified minds who are freed from from doubt.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even those who have all the knowledge which can be attained by the five senses, will derive no benefit from it, if they are without a knowledge of the true nature of things.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (True) knowledge is the perception concerning every thing of whatever kind, that that thing is the true thing.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They, who in this birth have learned to know the True Being, enter the road which returns not into this world.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let it not be thought that there is another birth for him whose mind having thoroughly considered (all it has been taught) has known the True Being.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: True knowledge consists in the removal of ignorance; which is (the cause of) births, and the perception of the True Being who is (the bestower of) heaven.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who so lives as to know Him who is the support of all things and abandon all desire, will be freed from the evils which would otherwise cleave to him and destroy (his efforts after absorption).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the very names of these three things, desire, anger, and confusion of mind, be destroyed, then will also perish the evils (which flow from them).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The wise) say that the seed, which produces unceasing births, at all times, to all creatures, is desire.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If anything be desired, freedom from births should be desired; that (freedom from births) will be attained by desiring to be without desire.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is in this world no excellence equal to freedom from desire; and even in that world, there is nothing like it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Purity (of mind) consists in freedom from desire; and that (freedom from desire) is the fruit of the love of truth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They are said to be free (from future birth) who are freed from desire; all others (who, whatever else they may be free from, are not freed from desire) are not thus free.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is the chief duty of (an ascetic) to watch against desire with (jealous) fear; for it has power to deceive (and destroy) him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a man thoroughly cut off all desire, the deeds, which confer immortality, will come to him, in the path in which he seeks them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is no sorrow to those who are without desire; but where that is, (sorrow) will incessantly come, more and more.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even while in this body, joy will never depart (from the mind, in which) desire, that sorrow of sorrows, has been destroyed.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The removal of desire, whose nature it is never to be satisfied, will immediately confer a nature that can never be changed.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Perseverance comes from a prosperous fate, and idleness from an adverse fate.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: An adverse fate produces folly, and a prosperous fate produces enlarged knowledge.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although (a man) may study the most polished treatises, the knowledge which fate has decreed to him will still prevail.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There are (through fate) two different natures in the world, hence the difference (observable in men) in (their acquisition of) wealth, and in their attainment of knowledge.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let In the acquisition of property, every thing favourable becomes unfavourable, and (on the other hand) everything unfavourable becomes favourable, (through the power of fate).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Whatever is not conferred by fate cannot be preserved although it be guarded with most painful care; and that, which fate has made his, cannot be lost, although one should even take it and throw it away.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even those who gather together millions will only enjoy them, as it has been determined by the disposer (of all things).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The destitute will renounce desire (and become ascetics), if (fate) do not make them suffer the hindrances to which they are liable, and they pass away.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: How is it that those, who are pleased with good fortune, trouble themselves when evil comes, (since both are equally the decree of fate) ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What is stronger than fate ? If we think of an expedient (to avert it), it will itself be with us before (the thought).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who possesses these six things, an army, a people, wealth, ministers, friends and a fortress, is a lion among kings.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Never to fail in these four things, fearlessness, liberality, wisdom, and energy, is the kingly character.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: These three things, viz., vigilance, learning, and bravery, should never be wanting in the ruler of a country.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is a king who, with manly modesty, swerves not from virtue, and refrains from vice.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is a king who is able to acquire (wealth), to lay it up, to guard, and to distribute it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The whole world will exalt the country of the king who is easy of access, and who is free from harsh language.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The world will praise and submit itself to the mind of the king who is able to give with affability, and to protect all who come to him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That king, will be esteemed a God among men, who performs his own duties, and protects (his subjects).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The whole world will dwell under the umbrella of the king, who can bear words that embitter the ear.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is the light of kings who has there four things, beneficence, benevolence, rectitude, and care for his people.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a man learn thoroughly whatever he may learn, and let his conduct be worthy of his learning.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Letters and numbers are the two eyes of man.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The learned are said to have eyes, but the unlearned have (merely) two sores in their face.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is the part of the learned to give joy to those whom they meet, and on leaving, to make them think (Oh! when shall we meet them again).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The unlearned are inferior to the learned, before whom they stand begging, as the destitute before the wealthy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Water will flow from a well in the sand in proportion to the depth to which it is dug, and knowledge will flow from a man in proportion to his learning.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: How is it that any one can remain without learning, even to his death, when (to the learned man) every country is his own (country), and every town his own (town) ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The learning, which a man has acquired in one birth, will yield him pleasure during seven births.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The learned will long (for more learning), when they see that while it gives pleasure to themselves, the world also derives pleasure from it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Learning is the true imperishable riches; all other things are not riches.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To speak in an assembly (of the learned) without fullness of knowledge, is like playing at chess (on a board) without squares.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The desire of the unlearned to speak (in an assembly), is like a woman without breasts desiring (the enjoyment of ) woman-hood.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The unlearned also are very excellent men, if they know how to keep silence before the learned.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although the natural knowledge of an unlearned man may be very good, the wise will not accept for true knowledge.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The self-conceit of an unlearned man will fade away, as soon as he speaks in an assembly (of the learned).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The unlearned are like worthless barren land: all that can be said of them is, that they exist.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The beauty and goodness of one who is destitute of knowledge by the study of great and exquisite works, is like (the beauty and goodness) of a painted earthen doll.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Wealth, gained by the unlearned, will give more sorrow than the poverty which may come upon the learned.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The unlearned, though born in a high caste, are not equal in dignity to the learned; though they may have been born in a low caste.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As beasts by the side of men, so are other men by the side of those who are learned in celebrated works.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Wealth (gained) by the ear is wealth of wealth; that wealth is the chief of all wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When there is no food for the ear, give a little also to the stomach.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who in this world enjoy instruction which is the food of the ear, are equal to the Gods, who enjoy the food of the sacrifices.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although a man be without learning, let him listen (to the teaching of the learned); that will be to him a staff in adversity.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The words of the good are like a staff in a slippery place.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a man listen, never so little, to good (instruction), even that will bring him great dignity.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not even when they have imperfectly understood (a matter), will those men speak foolishly, who have profoundly studied and diligently listened (to instruction).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The ear which has not been bored by instruction, although it hears, is deaf.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is a rare thing to find modesty, a reverend mouth- with those who have not received choice instruction.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What does it matter whether those men live or die, who can judge of tastes by the mouth, and not by the ear ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Wisdom is a weapon to ward off destruction; it is an inner fortress which enemies cannot destroy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not to permit the mind to go where it lists, to keep it from evil, and to employ it in good, this is wisdom.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To discern the truth in every thing, by whomsoever spoken, is wisdom.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To speak so as that the meaning may easily enter the mind of the hearer, and to discern the subtlest thought which may lie hidden in the words of others, this is wisdom.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To secure the friendship of the great is true wisdom; it is (also) wisdom to keep (that friendship unchanged, and) not opening and closing (like the lotus flower).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To live as the world lives, is wisdom.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wise are those who know beforehand what will happen; those who do not know this are the unwise.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not to fear what ought to be feared, is folly; it is the work of the wise to fear what should be feared.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: No terrifying calamity will happen to the wise, who (foresee) and guard against coming evils.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who possess wisdom, possess every thing; those who have not wisdom, whatever they may possess, have nothing.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Truly great is the excellence of those (kings) who are free from pride, anger, and lust.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Avarice, undignified pride, and low pleasures are faults in a king.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who fear guilt, if they commit a fault small as a millet seed, will consider it to be as large as a palmyra tree.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Guard against faults as a matter (of great consequence; for) faults are a deadly enemy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The prosperity of him who does not timely guard against faults, will perish like straw before fire.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What fault will remain in the king who has put away his own evils, and looks after the evils of others.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth of the avaricious man, who does not expend it for the purposes for which he ought to expend it will waste away and not continue.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Griping avarice is not to be reckoned as one among other faults; (it stands alone - greater than all).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let no (one) praise himself, at any time; let him not desire to do useless things.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If (a king) enjoys, privately the things which he desires, the designs of his enemies will be useless.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (a king) ponder well its value, and secure the friendship of men of virtue and of mature knowledge.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (a king) procure and kindly care for men who can overcome difficulties when they occur, and guard against them before they happen.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To cherish great men and make them his own, is the most difficult of all difficult things.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: So to act as to make those men, his own, who are greater than himself is of all powers the highest.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As a king must use his ministers as eyes (in managing his kingdom), let him well examine their character and qualifications before he engages them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There will be nothing left for enemies to do, against him who has the power of acting (so as to secure) the fellowship of worthy men.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Who are great enough to destroy him who has servants that have power to rebuke him ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The king, who is without the guard of men who can rebuke him, will perish, even though there be no one to destroy him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The There can be no gain to those who have no capital; and in like manner there can be no permanence to those who are without the support of adherents.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is tenfold more injurious to abandon the friendship of the good, than to incur the hatred of the many.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (True) greatness fears the society of the base; it is only the low - minded who will regard them as friends.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As water changes (its nature), from the nature of the soil (in which it flows), so will the character of men resemble that of their associates.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The power of knowing is from the mind; (but) his character is from that of his associates.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Wisdom appears to rest in the mind, but it really exists to a man in his companions.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Chaste company is the staff on which come, these two things, viz, purity of mind and purity of conduct.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To the pure-minded there will be a good posterity. By those whose associates are pure, no deeds will be done that are not good.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Goodness of mind will give wealth, and good society will bring with it all praise, to men.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although they may have great (natural) goodness of mind, yet good society will tend to strengthen it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Future bliss is (the result) of goodness of mind; and even this acquires strength from the society of the good.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is no greater help than the company of the good; there is no greater source of sorrow than the company of the wicked.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a man reflect on what will be lost, what will be acquired and (from these) what will be his ultimate gain, and (then, let him) act.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is nothing too difficult to (be attained by) those who, before they act, reflect well themselves, and thoroughly consider (the matter) with chosen friends.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The Wise men will not, in the hopes of profit, undertake works that will consume their principal.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who fear reproach will not commence anything which has not been (thoroughly considered) and made clear to them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: One way to promote the prosperity of an enemy, is (for a king) to set out (to war) without having thoroughly weighed his ability (to cope with its chances).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He will perish who does not what is not fit to do; and he also will perish who does not do what it is fit to do.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Consider, and then undertake a matter; after having undertaken it, to say "We will consider," is folly.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The work, which is not done by suitable methods, will fail though many stand to uphold it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There are failures even in acting well, when it is done without knowing the various dispositions of men.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a man reflect, and do things which bring no reproach; the world will not approve, with him, of things which do not become of his position to adopt.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (one) weigh well the strength of the deed (he purposes to do), his own strength, the strength of his enemy, and the strength of the allies (of both), and then let him act.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is nothing which may not be accomplished by those who, before they attack (an enemy), make themselves acquainted with their own ability, and with whatever else is (needful) to be known, and apply themselves wholly to their object.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There are many who, ignorant of their (want of) power (to meet it), have haughtily set out to war, and broken down in the midst of it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He will quickly perish who, ignorant of his own resources flatters himself of his greatness, and does not live in peace with his neighbours.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The axle tree of a bandy, loaded only with peacocks' feathers will break, if it be greatly overloaded.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There will be an end to the life of him who, having climbed out to the end of a branch, ventures to go further.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a man know the measure of his ability (to give), and let him give accordingly; such giving is the way to preserve his property.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even though the income (of a king) be small, it will not cause his (ruin), if his outgoings be not larger than his income.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The prosperity of him who lives without knowing the measure (of his property), will perish, even while it seems to continue.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The measure of his wealth will quickly perish, whose liberality weighs not the measure of his property.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A crow will overcome an owl in the day time; so the king who would conquer his enemy must have (a suitable) time.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Acting at the right season, is a cord that will immoveably bind success (to a king).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is there anything difficult for him to do, who acts, with (the right) instruments at the right time ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though (a man) should meditate (the conquest of) the world, he may accomplish it if he acts in the right time, and at the right place.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They who thoughtfully consider and wait for the (right) time (for action), may successfully meditate (the conquest of) the world.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The self-restraint of the energetic (while waiting for a suitable opportunity), is like the drawing back of a fighting-ram in order to butt.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wise will not immediately and hastily shew out their anger; they will watch their time, and restrain it within.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If one meets his enemy, let him show him all respect, until the time for his destruction is come; when that is come, his head will be easily brought low.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a rare opportunity occurs, while it lasts, let a man do that which is rarely to be accomplished (but for such an opportunity).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: At the time when one should use self-control, let him restrain himself like a heron; and, let him like it, strike, when there is a favourable opportunity.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let not (a king) despise (an enemy), nor undertake any thing (against him), until he has obtained (a suitable) place for besieging him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even to those who are men of power and expedients, an attack in connection with a fortification will yield many advantages.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even the powerless will become powerful and conquer, if they select a proper field (of action), and guard themselves, while they make war on their enemies.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If they who draw near (to fight) choose a suitable place to approach (their enemy), the latter, will have to relinquish the thought which they once entertained, of conquering them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In deep water, a crocodile will conquer (all other animals); but if it leave the water, other animals will conquer it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Wide chariots, with mighty wheels, will not run on the ocean; neither will ships that the traverse ocean, move on the earth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: You will need no other aid than fearlessness, if you thoroughly reflect (on what you are to do), and select (a suitable) place for your operations.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The power of one who has a large army will perish, if he goes into ground where only a small army can act.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is a hazardous thing to attack men in their own country, although they may neither have power nor a good fortress.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A fox can kill a fearless, warrior-faced elephant, if it go into mud in which its legs sink down.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (a minister) be chosen, after he has been tried by means of these four things, viz,-his virtue, (love of) money, (love of) sexual pleasure, and tear of (losing) life.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The king's) choice should (fall) on him, who is of good family, who is free from faults, and who has the modesty which fears the wounds (of sin).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When even men, who have studied the most difficult works, and who are free from faults, are (carefully) examined, it is a rare thing to find them without ignorance.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (a king) consider (a man's) good qualities, as well as his faults, and then judge (of his character) by that which prevails.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A man's deeds are the touchstone of his greatness and littleness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (a king) avoid choosing men who have no relations; such men have no attachment, and therefore have no fear of crime.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To choose ignorant men, through partiality, is the height of folly.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sorrow that will not leave even his posterity will come upon him chooses a stranger whose character he has not known.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (a king) choose no one without previous consideration; after he has made his choice, let him unhesitatingly select for each such duties as are appropriate.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To make choice of one who has not been examined, and to entertain doubts respecting one who has been chosen, will produce irremediable sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He should be employed (by a king), whose nature leads him to choose the good, after having weighed both the evil and the good in any undertaking.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let him do (the king's) work who can enlarge the sources (of revenue), increase wealth and considerately prevent the accidents (which would destroy it).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let the choice (of a king) fall upon him who largely possesses these four things, love, knowledge, a clear mind and freedom from covetousness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even when (a king) has tried them in every possible way, there are many men who change, from the nature of the works (in which they may be employed).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (A king's) work can only be accomplished by a man of wisdom and patient endurance; it is not of a nature to be given to one from mere personal attachment.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (a king) act, after having considered the agent (whom he is to employ), the deed (he desires to do), and the time which is suitable to it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: After having considered, "this man can accomplish this, by these means", let (the king) leave with him the discharge of that duty.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Having considered what work a man is fit for, let (the king) employ him in that work.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Prosperity will leave (the king) who doubts the friendship of the man who steadily labours in the discharge of his duties.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a king daily examine the conduct of his servants; if they do not act crookedly, the world will not act crookedly.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even when (a man's) property is all gone, relatives will act towards him with their accustomed (kindness).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If (a man's) relatives remain attached to him with unchanging love, it will be a source of ever-increasing wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth of one who does not mingle freely with his relatives, will be like the filling of water in a spacious tank that has no banks.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To live surrounded by relatives, is the advantage to be derived from the acquisition of wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He will be surrounded by numerous relatives who manifests generosity and affability.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: No one, in all the world, will have so many relatives (about him), as he who makes large gift, and does not give way to anger.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The crows do not conceal (their prey), but will call out for others (to share with them) while they eat it; wealth will be with those who show a similar disposition (towards their relatives).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Many relatives will live near a king, when they observe that he does not look on all alike, but that he looks on each man according to his merit.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who have been friends and have afterwards forsaken him, will return and join themselves (to him), when the cause of disagreement is not to be found in him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When one may have left him, and for some cause has returned to him, let the king fulfil the object (for which he has come back) and thoughtfully receive him again.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: More evil than excessive anger, is forgetfulness which springs from the intoxication of great joy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Forgetfulness will destroy fame, even as constant poverty destroys knowledge.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Thoughtlessness will never acquire fame; and this tenet is upheld by all treatises in the world.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Just as the coward has no defence (by whatever fortifications ha may be surrounded), so the thoughtless has no good (whatever advantages he may possess).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The thoughtless man, who provides not against the calamities that may happen, will afterwards repent for his fault.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is nothing comparable with the possession of unfailing thoughtfulness at all times; and towards all persons.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is nothing too difficult to be accomplished, if a man set about it carefully, with unflinching endeavour.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (a man) observe and do these things which have been praised (by the wise); if he neglects and fails to perform them, for him there will be no (happiness) throughout the seven births.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (a king) think of those who have been ruined by neglect, when his mind is elated with joy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is easy for (one) to obtain whatever he may think of, if he can again think of it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To examine into (the crimes which may be committed), to show no favour (to any one), to desire to act with impartiality towards all, and to inflict (such punishments) as may be wisely resolved on, constitute rectitude.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When there is rain, the living creation thrives; and so when the king rules justly, his subjects thrive.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The sceptre of the king is the firm support of the Vedas of the Brahmin, and of all virtues therein described.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The world will constantly embrace the feet of the great king who rules over his subjects with love.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Rain and plentiful crops will ever dwell together in the country of the king who sways his sceptre with justice.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is not the javelin that gives victory, but the king's sceptre, if it do no injustice.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The king defends the whole world; and justice, when administered without defect, defends the king.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The king who gives not facile audience (to those who approach him), and who does not examine and pass judgment (on their complaints), will perish in disgrace.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In guarding his subjects (against injury from others), and in preserving them himself; to punish crime is not a fault in a king, but a duty.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: For a king to punish criminals with death, is like pulling up the weeds in the green corn.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The king who gives himself up to oppression and acts unjustly (towards his subjects) is more cruel than the man who leads the life of a murderer.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The request (for money) of him who holds the sceptre is like the word of a highway robber who stands with a weapon in hand and says "give up your wealth".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The country of the king who does not daily examine into the wrongs done and distribute justice, will daily fall to ruin
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The king, who, without reflecting (on its evil consequences), perverts justice, will lose at once both his wealth and his subjects.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Will not the tears, shed by a people who cannot endure the oppression which they suffer (from their king), become a saw to waste away his wealth ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Righteous government gives permanence to (the fame of) kings; without that their fame will have no endurance.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As is the world without rain, so live a people whose king is without kindness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Property gives more sorrow than poverty, to those who live under the sceptre of a king without justice.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the king acts contrary to justice, rain will become unseasonable, and the heavens will withhold their showers.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the guardian (of the country) neglects to guard it, the produce of the cows will fail, and the men of six duties viz., the Brahmins will forget the vedas.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is a king who having equitably examined (any injustice which has been brought to his notice), suitably punishes it, so that it may not be again committed.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let the king, who desires that his prosperity may long remain, commence his preliminary enquires with strictness, and then punish with mildness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The cruel-sceptred king, who acts so as to put his subjects in fear, will certainly and quickly come to ruin.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The king who is spoken of as cruel will quickly perish; his life becoming shortened.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The great wealth of him who is difficult of access and possesses a sternness of countenance, is like that which has been obtained by a devil.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The abundant wealth of the king whose words are harsh and whose looks are void of kindness, will instantly perish instead of abiding long, with him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Severe words and excessive punishments will be a file to waste away a king's power for destroying (his enemies).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The prosperity of that king will waste away, who without reflecting (on his affairs himself), commits them to his ministers, and (when a failure occurs) gives way to anger, and rages against them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The king who has not provided himself with a place of defence, will in times of war be seized with fear and quickly perish.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The earth bears up no greater burden than ignorant men whom a cruel sceptre attaches to itself (as the ministers of its evil deeds).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The world exists through that greatest ornament (of princes), a gracious demeanour.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The prosperity of the world springs from the kindliness, the existence of those who have no (kindliness) is a burden to the earth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Of what avail is a song if it be inconsistent with harmony ? what is the use of eyes which possess no kindliness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Beyond appearing to be in the face, what good do they do, those eyes in which is no well-regulated kindness ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Kind looks are the ornaments of the eyes; without these they will be considered (by the wise) to be merely two sores.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He They resemble the trees of the earth, who although they have eyes, never look kindly (on others).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Men without kind looks are men without eyes; those who (really) have eyes are also not devoid of kind looks.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The world is theirs (kings) who are able to show kindness, without injury to their affairs, (administration of justice).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Patiently to bear with, and show kindness to those who grieve us, is the most excellent of all dispositions.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who desire (to cultivate that degree of) urbanity which all shall love, even after swallowing the poison served to them by their friends, will be friendly with them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a king consider as his eyes these two things, a spy and a book (of laws) universally esteemed.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is the duty of a king to know quickly (by a spy) what all happens, daily, amongst all men.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is no way for a king to obtain conquests, who knows not the advantage of discoveries made by a spy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is a spy who watches all men, to wit, those who are in the king's employment, his relatives, and his enemies.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A spy is one who is able to assume an appearance which may create no suspicion (in the minds of others), who fears no man's face, and who never reveals (his purpose).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is a spy who, assuming the appearance of an ascetic, goes into (whatever place he wishes), examines into (all, that is needful), and never discovers himself, whatever may be done to him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A spy is one who is able to discover what is hidden and who retains no doubt concerning what he has known.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let not a king receive the information which a spy has discovered and made known to him, until he has examined it by another spy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a king employ spies so that one may have no knowledge of the other; and when the information of three agrees together, let him receive it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let not a king publicly confer on a spy any marks of his favour; if he does, he will divulge his own secret.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Energy makes out the man of property; as for those who are destitute of it, do they (really) possess what they possess ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The possession of (energy of) mind is true property; the possession of wealth passes away and abides not.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They who are possessed of enduring energy will not trouble themselves, saying, "we have lost our property".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Wealth will find its own way to the man of unfailing energy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The stalks of water-flowers are proportionate to the depth of water; so is men's greatness proportionate to their minds.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In all that a king thinks of, let him think of his greatness; and if it should be thrust from him (by fate), it will have the nature of not being thrust from him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The strong minded will not faint, even when all is lost; the elephant stands firm, even when wounded by a shower of arrows.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who have no (greatness of) mind, will not acquire the joy of saying in the world, "we have excercised liaberality".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although the elephant has a large body, and a sharp tusk, yet it fears the attack of the tiger.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Energy is mental wealth; those men who are destitute of it are only trees in the form of men.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
