work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: By the darkness, of idleness, the indestructible lamp of family (rank) will be extinguished.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let those, who desire that their family may be illustrious, put away all idleness from their conduct.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The (lustre of the) family of the ignorant man, who acts under the influence of destructive laziness will perish, even before he is dead.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Family (greatness) will be destroyed, and faults will increase, in those men who give way to laziness, and put forth no dignified exertions.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Procrastination, forgetfulness, idleness, and sleep, these four things, form the vessel which is desired by those destined to destruction.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is a rare thing for the idle, even when possessed of the riches of kings who ruled over the whole earth, to derive any great benefit from it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who through idleness, and do not engage themselves in dignified exertion, will subject themselves to rebukes and reproaches.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If idleness take up its abode in a king of high birth, it will make him a slave of his enemies.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When a man puts away idleness, the reproach which has come upon himself and his family will disappear.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The king who never gives way to idleness will obtain entire possession of (the whole earth) passed over by him who measured (the worlds) with His foot.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Yield not to the feebleness which says, "this is too difficult to be done"; labour will give the greatness (of mind) which is necessary (to do it).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Take care not to give up exertion in the midst of a work; the world will abandon those who abandon their unfinished work.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The lustre of munificence will dwell only with the dignity of laboriousness or efforts.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The liberality of him, who does not labour, will fail, like the manliness of a hermaphrodite, who has a sword in its hand.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who desires not pleasure, but desires labour, will be a pillar to sustain his relations, wiping away their sorrows.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Labour will produce wealth; idleness will bring poverty.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They say that the black Mudevi (the goddess of adversity) dwells with laziness, and the Latchmi (the goddess of prosperity) dwells with the labour of the industrious.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Adverse fate is no disgrace to any one; to be without exertion and without knowing what should be known, is disgrace.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although it be said that, through fate, it cannot be attained, yet labour, with bodily exertion, will yield its reward.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They who labour on, without fear and without fainting will see even fate (put) behind their back.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If troubles come, laugh; there is nothing like that, to press upon and drive away sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A flood of troubles will be overcome by the (courageous) thought which the minds of the wise will entertain, even in sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They give sorrow to sorrow, who in sorrow do not suffer sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Troubles will vanish (i.e., will be troubled) before the man who (struggles against difficulties) as a buffalo (drawing a cart) through deep mire.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The troubles of that man will be troubled (and disappear) who, however thickly they may come upon him, does not abandon (his purpose).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Will those men ever cry out in sorrow, "we are destitute" who, (in their prosperity), give not way to (undue desire) to keep their wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The great will not regard trouble as trouble, knowing that the body is the butt of trouble.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That man never experiences sorrow, who does not seek for pleasure, and who considers distress to be natural (to man).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He does not suffer sorrow, in sorrow who does not look for pleasure in pleasure.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The elevation, which even his enemies will esteem, will be gained by him, who regards pain as pleasure.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The minister is one who can make an excellent choice of means, time, manner of execution, and the difficult undertaking (itself).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The minister is one who in addition to the aforesaid five things excels in the possession of firmness, protection of subjects, clearness by learning, and perseverance.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The minister is one who can effect discord (among foes), maintain the good-will of his friends and restore to friendship those who have seceded (from him).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The minister is one who is able to comprehend (the whole nature of an undertaking), execute it in the best manner possible, and offer assuring advice (in time of necessity).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is the best helper (of the king) who understanding the duties, of the latter, is by his special learning, able to tender the fullest advice, and at all times conversant with the best method (of performing actions).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What (contrivances) are there so acute as to resist those who possess natural acuteness in addition to learning ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though you are acquainted with the (theoretical) methods (of performing an act), understand the ways of the world and act accordingly.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although the king be utterly ignorant, it is the duty of the minister to give (him) sound advice.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Far better are seventy crores of enemies (for a king) than a minister at his side who intends (his) ruin.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those ministers who are destitute of (executive) ability will fail to carry out their projects, although they may have contrived aright.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The possession of that goodness which is called the goodness of speech is (even to others) better than any other goodness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Since (both) wealth and evil result from (their) speech, ministers should most carefully guard themselves against faultiness therein.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The (minister's) speech is that which seeks (to express) elements as bind his friends (to himself) and is so delivered as to make even his enemies desire (his friendship).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Understand the qualities (of your hearers) and (then) make your speech; for superior to it, there is neither virtue nor wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Deliver your speech, after assuring yourself that no counter speech can defeat your own.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is the opinion of those who are free from defects in diplomacy that the minister should speak so as to make his hearers desire (to hear more) and grasp the meaning of what he hears himself.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is impossible for any one to conquer him by intrique who possesses power of speech, and is neither faulty nor timid.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If there be those who can speak on various subjects in their proper order and in a pleasing manner, the world would readily accept them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They will desire to utter many words, who do not know how to speak a few faultless ones.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who are unable to set forth their acquirements (before others) are like flowers blossoming in a cluster and yet without fragrance.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The efficacy of support will yield (only) wealth; (but) the efficacy of action will yield all that is desired.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Ministers should at all times avoid acts which, in addition to fame, yield no benefit (for the future).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who say, "we will become (better)" should avoid the performance of acts that would destroy (their fame).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who have infallible judgement though threatened with peril will not do acts which have brought disgrace (on former ministers).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let a minister never do acts of which he would have to grieve saying, "what is this I have done"; (but) should he do (them), it were good that he grieved not.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though a minister may see his mother starve; let him do not act which the wise would (treat with contempt).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Far more excellent is the extreme poverty of the wise than wealth obtained by heaping up of sinful deeds.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The actions of those, who have not desisted from doing deeds forbidden (by the great), will, even if they succeed, cause them sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: All that has been obtained with tears (to the victim) will depart with tears (to himself); but what has been by fair means; though with loss at first, will afterwards yield fruit.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (For a minister) to protect (his king) with wealth obtained by foul means is like preserving a vessel of wet clay by filling it with water.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Firmness in action is (simply) one's firmness of mind; all other (abilities) are not of this nature.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not to perform a ruinous act, and not to be discouraged by the ruinous termination of an act, are the two maxims which, the wise say, from the principles of those who have investigated the subject.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: So to perform an act as to publish it (only) at its termination is (true) manliness; for to announce it beforehand, will cause irremediable sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To say (how an act is to be performed) is (indeed) easy for any one; but far difficult it is to do according to what has been said.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The firmness in action of those who have become great by the excellence (of their counsel) will, by attaining its fulfilment in the person of the king, be esteemed (by all).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If those who have planned (an undertaking) possess firmness (in executing it) they will obtain what they have desired even as they have desired it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let none be despised for (their) size; (for) the world has those who resemble the linch-pin of the big rolling car.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: An act that has been firmly resolved on must be as firmly carried out without delay.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though it should cause increasing sorrow (at the outset), do with firmness the act that yield bliss (in the end)
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The great will not esteem those who esteem not firmness of action, whatever other abilities the latter may possess.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Consultation ends in forming a resolution (to act); (but) delay in the execution of that resolve is an evil.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sleep over such (actions) as may be slept over; (but) never over such as may not be slept over.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Whenever it is possible (to overcome your enemy) the act (of fighting) is certainly good; if not, endeavour to employ some more successful method.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When duly considered, the incomplete execution of an undertaking and hostility will grow and destroy one like the (unextinguished) remnant of a fire.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Do an act after a due consideration of the (following) five, viz. money, means, time, execution and place.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: An act is to be performed after considering the exertion required, the obstacles to be encountered, and the great profit to be gained (on its completion).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The method of performance for one who has begun an act is to ascertain the mind of him who knows the secret thereof.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To make one undertaking the means of accomplishing another (similar to it) is like making one rutting elephant the means of capturing another.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: One should rather hasten to secure the alliance of the foes (of one's foes) than perform good offices to one's friends.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Ministers of small states, afraid of their people being frightened, will yield to and acknowledge their superior foes, if the latter offer them a chance of reconciliation.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The qualification of an ambassador are affection (for his relations) a fitting birth, and the possession of attributes pleasing to royalty.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Love (to his sovereign), knowledge (of his affairs), and a discriminating power of speech (before other sovereigns) are the three sine qua non qualifications of an ambassador.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To be powerful in politics among those who are learned (in ethics) is the character of him who speaks to lance-bearing kings on matters of triumph (to his own sovereign).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He may go on a mission (to foreign rulers) who has combined in him all these three. viz., (natural) sense, an attractive bearing and well-tried learning.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is an ambassador who (in the presence of foreign rulers) speaks briefly, avoids harshness, talks so as to make them smile, and thus brings good (to his own sovereign).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is an ambassador who having studied (politics) talks impressively, is not afraid of angry looks, and knows (to employ) the art suited to the time.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is chief (among ambassadors) who understands the proper decorum (before foreign princes), seeks the (proper) occasion, knows the (most suitable) place, and delivers his message after (due) consideration.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The qualifications of him who faithfully delivers his (sovereign's) message are purity, the support (of foreign ministers), and boldness, with truthfulness in addition to the (aforesaid) three.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He alone is fit to communicate (his sovereign's) reply, who possesses the firmness not to utter even inadvertently what may reflect discredit (on the latter).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is the ambassador who fearlessly seeks his sovereign's good though it should cost him his life (to deliver his message).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Ministers who serve under fickle-minded monarchs should, like those who warm themselves at the fire, be neither (too) far, nor (too) near.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: For ministers not to cover the things desired by their kings will through the kings themselves yield them everlasting wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Ministers who would save themselves should avoid (the commission of) serious errors for if the king's suspicion is once roused, no one can remove it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: While in the presence of the sovereign, ministers should neither whisper to nor smile at others.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (When the king is engaged) in secret counsel (with others), ministers should neither over-hear anything whatever nor pry into it with inquisitive questions, but (wait to) listen when it is divulged (by the king himself).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Knowing the (king's disposition and seeking the right time, (the minister) should in a pleasing manner suggest things such as are desirable and not disagreeable.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Ministers should (always) give agreeable advice but on no occasion recommend useless actions, though requested (to do so).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Ministers should behave in accordance with the (Divine) light in the person of kings and not despise them saying, "He is our junior (in age) and connected with our family!".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those whose judgement is firm will not do what is disagreeable (to the sovereign) saying (within themselves) "We are esteemed by the king".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The (foolish) claim with which a minister does unbecoming acts because of his (long) familiarity (with the king) will ensure his ruin.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The minister who by looking (at the king) understands his mind without being told (of it), will be a perpetual ornament to the world which is surrounded by a never-drying sea.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is to be esteemed a god who is able to ascertain without a doubt what is within (one's mind).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The king should ever give whatever (is asked) of his belongings and secure him who, by the indications (of his own mind) is able to read those of another.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who understand one's thoughts without being informed (thereof) and those who do not, may (indeed) resemble one another bodily; still are they different (mentally).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Of what use are the eyes amongst one's members, if they cannot by their own indications dive those of another ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As the mirror reflects what is near so does the face show what is uppermost in the mind.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is there anything so full of knowledge as the face ? (No.) it precedes the mind, whether (the latter is) pleased or vexed.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the king gets those who by looking into his mind can understand (and remove) what has occurred (to him) it is enough that he stand looking at their face.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a king gets ministers who can read the movements of the eye, the eyes (of foreign kings) will (themselves) reveal (to him) their hatred or friendship.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The measuring-rod of those (ministers) who say "we are acute" will on inquiry be found to be their (own) eyes and nothing else.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let the pure who know the arrangement of words speak with deliberation after ascertaining (the nature of) the court (then assembled).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let the good who know the uses of words speak with a clear knowledge after ascertaining the time (suited to the court).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who undertake to speak without knowing the (nature of the) court are ignorant of the quality of words as well as devoid of the power (of learning).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Ministers should be lights in the assembly of the enlightned, but assume the pure whiteness of mortar (ignorance) in that of fools.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The modesty by which one does not rush forward and speak in (an assembly of) superiors is the best among all (one's) good qualities.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (For a minister) to blunder in the presence of those who have acquired a vast store of learning and know (the value thereof) is like a good man stumbling (and falling away) from the path (of virtue).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The learning of those who have read and understood (much) will shine in the assembly of those who faultlessly examine (the nature of) words.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Lecturing to those who have the ability to understand (for themselves) is like watering a bed of plants that are growing (of themselves).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who are able to speak good things impressively in an assembly of the good should not even forgetfully speak them in that of the low.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To utter (a good word) in the assembly of those who are of inferior rank is like dropping nectar on the ground.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The pure who know the classification of words having first ascertained the nature (of the court) will not (through fear) falter in their speech before the powerful body.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who can agreeably set forth their acquirements before the learned will be regarded as the most learned among the learned.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Many indeed may (fearlessly) die in the presence of (their) foes; (but) few are those who are fearless in the assembly (of the learned).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (Ministers) should agreeably set forth their acquirements before the learned and acquire more (knowledge) from their superiors (in learning).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In order to reply fearlessly before a foreign court, (ministers) should learn logic according to the rules (of grammar).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What have they to do with a sword who are not valiant, or they with learning who are afraid of an intelligent assembly ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The learning of him who is diffident before an assembly is like the shining sword of an hermaphrodite in the presence of his foes.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who cannot agreeably speak good things before a good assembly are indeed unprofitable persons inspite of all their various acquirements.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They who, though they have learned and understood, are yet afraid of the assembly of the good, are said to be inferior (even) to the illiterate.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who through fear of the assembly are unable to set forth their learning in an interesting manner, though alive, are yet like the dead.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A kingdom is that in which (those who carry on) a complete cultivation, virtuous persons, and merchants with inexhaustible wealth, dwell together.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A kingdom is that which is desire for its immense wealth, and which grows greatly in prosperity, being free from destructive causes.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A kingdom is that which can bear any burden that may be pressed on it (from adjoining kingdoms) and (yet) pay the full tribute to its sovereign.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: kingdom is that which continues to be free from excessive starvation, irremediable epidemics, and destructive foes.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A kingdom is that which is without various (irregular) associations, destructive internal enemies, and murderous savages who (sometimes) harass the sovereign.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The learned say that the best kingdom is that which knows no evil (from its foes), and, if injured (at all), suffers no diminution in its fruitfulness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The constituents of a kingdom are the two waters (from above and below), well situated hills and an undestructible fort.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Freedom from epidemics, wealth, produce, happiness and protection (to subjects); these five, the learned, say, are the ornaments of a kingdom.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The learned say that those are kingdom whose wealth is not laboured for, and those not, whose wealth is only obtained through labour.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although in possession of all the above mentioned excellences, these are indeed of no use to a country, in the absence of harmony between the sovereign and the sujects.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A fort is an object of importance to those who march (against their foes) as well as to those who through fear (of pursuers) would seek it for shelter.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A fort is that which has everlasting water, plains, mountains and cool shady forests.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The learned say that a fortress is an enclosure having these four (qualities) viz., height, breadth, strength and inaccessibility.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A fort is that which has an extensive space within, but only small places to be guarded, and such as can destroy the courage of besieging foes.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A fort is that which cannot be captured, which abounds in suitable provisions, and affords a position of easy defence to its inmates.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A fort is that which has all (needful) things, and excellent heroes that can help it against destruction (by foes).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A fort is that which cannot be captured by blockading, assaulting, or undermining it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That is a fort whose inmates are able to overcome without losing their ground, even abler men who have besieged it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A fort is that which derives excellence from the stratagems made (by its inmates) to defeat their enemies in the battlefield.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although a fort may possess all (the above-said) excellence, it is, as it were without these, if its inmates possess not the excellence of action.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Besides wealth there is nothing that can change people of no importance into those of (some) importance.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: All despise the poor; (but) all praise the rich.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The imperishable light of wealth goes into regions desired (by its owner) and destroys the darkness (of enmity therein).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth acquired with a knowledge of the proper means and without foul practices will yield virtue and happiness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (Kings) should rather avoid than seek the accumulation of wealth which does not flow in with mercy and love.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Unclaimed wealth, wealth acquired by taxes, and wealth (got) by conquest of foes are (all) the wealth of the king.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The child mercy which is borne by love grows under the care of the rich nurse of wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: An undertaking of one who has wealth in one's hands is like viewing an elephant-fight from a hill-top.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Accumulate wealth; it will destroy the arrogance of (your) foes; there is no weapon sharper than it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To those who have honestly acquired an abundance of riches, the other two, (virtue and pleasure) are things easy (of acquisition).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The army which is complete in (its) parts and conquers without fear of wounds is the chief wealth of the king.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Ancient army can alone have the valour which makes it stand by its king at the time of defeat, fearless of wounds and unmindful of its reduced strength.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What if (a host of) hostile rats roar like the sea ? They will perish at the mere breath of the cobra.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That indeed is an army which has stood firm of old without suffering destruction or deserting (to the enemy).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That indeed is an army which is capable of offering a united resistance, even if Yama advances against it with fury.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Valour, honour, following in the excellent-footsteps (of its predecessors) and trust-worthiness; these four alone constitute the safeguard of an army
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: That is an army which knowing the art of warding off an impending struggle, can bear against the dust-van (of a hostile force).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though destitute of courage to fight and strength (to endure), an army may yet gain renown by the splendour of its appearance.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: An army can triumph (over its foes) if it is free from diminution; irremediable aversion and poverty.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though an army may contain a large number of permanent soldiers, it cannot last if it has no generals.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my foes, stand not before my leader; (for) many are those who did so but afterwards stood (in the shape of) statues.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is more pleasant to hold the dart that has missed an elephant than that which has hit hare in the forest.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The learned say that fierceness (incontest with a foe) is indeed great valour; but to become a benefactor in case of accident (to a foe) is the extreme (limit) of that valour.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The hero who after casting the lance in his hand on an elephant, comes (in search of another) will pluck the one (that sticks) in his body and laugh (exultingly).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is it not a defeat to the valiant to wink and destroy their ferocious look when a lance in cast at them (by their foe) ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The hero will reckon among wasted days all those on which he had not received severe wounds.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The fastening of ankle-ring by those who disire a world-wide renown and not (the safety of) their lives is like adorning (themselves).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The heroes who are not afraid of losing their life in a contest will not cool their ardour, even if the king prohibits (their fighting).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Who would reproach with failure those who seal their oath with their death ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If (heroes) can so die as to fill with tears the eyes of their rulers, such a death deserves to be obtained even by begging.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What things are there so difficult to acquire as friendship ? What guards are there so difficult to break through by the efforts (of one's foes) ? .
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The friendship of the wise waxes like the new moon; (but) that of fools wanes like the full moon.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Like learning, the friendship of the noble, the more it is cultivated, the more delightful does it become.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Friendship is to be practised not for the purpose of laughing but for that of being beforehand in giving one another sharp rebukes in case of transgression.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Living together and holding frequent intercourse are not necessary (for friendship); (mutual) understanding can alone create a claim for it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The love that dwells (merely in the smiles of the face is not friendship; (but) that which dwells deep in the smiles of the heart is true friendship.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (True) friendship turns aside from evil (ways) makes (him) walk in the (good) way, and, in case of loss if shares his sorrow (with him).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (True) friendship hastens to the rescue of the afflicted (as readily) as the hand of one whose garment is loosened (before an assembly).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Friendship may be said to be on its throne when it possesses the power of supporting one at all times and under all circumstances, (in the practice or virtue and wealth).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though friends may praise one another saying, "He is so intimate with us, and we so much (with him)"; (still) such friendship will appear mean.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As those who are of a friendly nature will not forsake (a friend) after once loving (him), there is no evil so great as contracting a friendship without due inquiry.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The friendship contracted by him who has not made repeated inquiry will in the end grieve (him) to death.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Make friendship (with one) after ascertaining (his) character, birth, defects and the whole of one's relations.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The friendship of one who belongs to a (good) family and is afraid of (being charged with) guilt, is worth even purchasing.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: You should examine and secure the friendship of those who can speak so as to make you weep over a crime (before its commission) or rebuke you severely (after you have done it) and are able to teach you (the ways of) the world.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even in ruin there is some good; (for) it is a rod by which one may measure fully (the affection of one's) relations.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is indead a gain for one to renounce the friendship of fools.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Do not think of things that discourage your mind, nor contract friendship with those who would forsake you in adversity.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The very thought of the friendship of those who have deserted one at the approach of adversity will burn one's mind at the time of death.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Continue to enjoy the friendship of the pure; (but) renounce even with a gift, the friendship of those who do not agree (with the world).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Imtimate friendship is that which cannot in the least be injured by (things done through the) right (of longstanding intimacy).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The constituents of friendship are (things done through) the right of intimacy; to be pleased with such a right is the duty of the wise.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Of what avail is long-standing friendship, if friends do not admit as their own actions done through the right of intimacy ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If friends, through the right of friendship, do (anything) without being asked, the wise will be pleased with them on account of its desirability.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If friends should perform what is painful, understand that it is owing not only to ignorance, but also to the strong claims of intimacy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who stand within the limits (of true friendship) will not even in adversity give up the intimacy of long-standing friends.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who have (long) stood in the path of affection will not give it up even if their friends cause (them) their ruin.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To those who understand that by which they should not listen to (tales about) the faults of their friends, that is a (profitable) day on which the latter may commit a fault.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They will be loved by the world, who have not forsaken the friendship of those with whom they have kept up an unbroken long-standing intimacy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even enemies will love those who have never changed in their affection to their long-standing friends.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The decrease of friendship with those who look as if they would eat you up (through excess of love) while they are really destitute of goodness is far better than its increase.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Of what avail is it to get or lose the friendship of those who love when there is gain and leave when there is none ? .
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Friendship who calculate the profits (of their friendship), prostitutes who are bent on obtaining their gains, and thieves are (all) of the same character.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Solitude is more to be desired than the society of those who resemble the untrained horses which throw down (their riders) in the fields of battle.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is far better to avoid that to contract the evil friendship of the base who cannot protect (their friends) even when appointed to do so.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The hatred of the wise is ten-million times more profitable than the excessive intimacy of the fool.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What comes from enemies is a hundred million times more profitable than what comes from the friendship of those who cause only laughter.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Gradually abandon without revealing (beforehand) the friendship of those who pretend inability to carry out what they (really) could do.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The friendship of those whose actions do not agree with their words will distress (one) even in (one's) dreams.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Avoid even the least approach to a contraction of friendship with those who would love you in private but ridicule you in public.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The friendship of those who behave like friends without inward affection is a weapon that may be thrown when a favourable opportunity presents itself.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The friendship of those who seem to be friends while they are not, will change like the love of women.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though (one's) enemies may have mastered many good books, it will be impossible for them to become truly loving at heart.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: One should fear the deceitful who smile sweetly with their face but never love with their heart.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In nothing whatever is it proper to rely on the words of those who do not love with their heart.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though (one's) foes may utter good things as though they were friends, once will at once understand (their evil, import).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Since the bending of the bow bespeaks evil, one should not accept (as good) the humiliating speeches of one's foes.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A weapon may be hid in the very hands with which (one's) foes adore (him) (and) the tears they shed are of the same nature.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is the duty of kings to affect great love but make it die (inwardly); as regard those foes who shew them great friendship but despise them (in their heart).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When one's foes begin to affect friendship, one should love them with one's looks, and, cherishing no love in the heart, give up (even the former).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Folly is one (of the chief defects); it is that which (makes one) incur loss and forego gain.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The greatest folly is that which leads one to take delight in doing what is forbidden.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Shamelessness indifference (to what must be sought after), harshness, and aversion for everything (that ought to be desired) are the qualities of the fool.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There are no greater fools than he who, though he has read and understood (a great deal) and even taught it to others, does not walk according to his own teaching.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A fool can procure in a single birth a hell into which he may enter and suffer through all the seven births.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the fool, who knows not how to act undertakes a work, he will (certainly) fail. (But) is it all ? He will even adorn himself with fetters.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a fool happens to get an immense fortune, his neighbours will enjoy it while his relations starve.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A fool happening to possess something is like the intoxication of one who is (already) giddy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The friendship between fools is exceedingly delightful (to each other): for at parting there will be nothing to cause them pain.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The appearance of a fool in an assembly of the learned is like placing (one's) unwashed feet on a bed.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The want of wisdom is the greatest of all wants; but that of wealth the world will not regard as such.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The cause of) a fool cheerfully giving (something) is nothing else but the receiver's merit (in a former birth).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The suffering that fools inflict upon themselves is hardly possible even to foes.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What is called want of wisdom is the vanity which says, "We are wise".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Fools pretending to know what has not been read (by them) will rouse suspicion even as to what they have thoroughly mastered.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even to cover one's nakedness would be folly, if (one's) faults were not covered (by forsaking them).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The fool who neglects precious counsel does, of his own accord, a great injury to himself.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The fool will not perform (his duties) even when advised nor ascertain them himself; such a soul is a burden (to the earth) till it departs (from the body).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: One who would teach a fool will (simply) betray his folly; and the fool would (still) think himself "wise in his own conceit".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who denies the existence of what the world believes in will be regarded as a demon on earth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The disease which fosters the evil of disunion among all creatures is termed hatred by the wise.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though disagreeable things may be done from (a feeling of) disunion, it is far better that nothing painful be done from (that of) hatred.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To rid one-self of the distressing dtsease of hatred will bestow (on one) a never-decreasing imperishable fame.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If hatred which is the greatest misery is destroyed, it will yield the greatest delight.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Who indeed would think of conquering those who naturally shrink back from hatred ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Failure and ruin are not far from him who says it is sweet to excel in hatred.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those whose judgement brings misery through its connection with hatred cannot understand the triumphant nature of truth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Shrinking back from hatred will yield wealth; indulging in its increase will hasten ruin.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: At the approach of wealth one will not think of hatred (but) to secure one's ruin, one will look to its increase.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: All calamities are caused by hatred; but by the delight (of friendship) is caused the great wealth of good virtues.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Avoid offering resistance to the strong; (but) never fail to cherish enmity towards the weak.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: How can he who is unloving, destitute of powerful aids, and himself without strength overcome the might of his foe ?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In the estimation of foes miserably weak is he, who is timid, ignorant, unsociable and niggardly.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who neither refrains from anger nor keeps his secrets will at all times and in all places be easily conquered by all.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (A) pleasing (object) to his foes is he who reads not moral works, does nothing that is enjoined by them cares not for reproach and is not possessed of good qualities.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Highly to be desired is the hatred of him whose anger is blind, and whose lust increases beyond measure.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is indeed necessary to obtain even by purchase the hatred of him who having begun (a work) does what is not conductive (to its accomplishment).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He will become friendless who is without (any good) qualities. and whose faults are many; (such a character) is a help to (his) foes.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There will be no end of lofty delights to the victorious, if their foes are (both) ignorant and timid.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The light (of fame) will never be gained by him who gains not the trifling reputation of having fought an unlearned (foe).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The evil of hatred is not of a nature to be desired by one even in sport.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though you may incur the hatred of warriors whose ploughs are bows, incur not that of ministers whose ploughs are words.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who being alone, incurs the hatred of many is more infatuated than even mad men.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The world abides in the greatness of that good-natured man who behaves so as to turn hatred into friendship.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who is alone and helpless while his foes are two should secure one of them as an agreeable help (to himself).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though (one's foe is) aware or not of one's misfortune one should act so as neither to join nor separate (from him).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Relate not your suffering even to friends who are ignorant of it, nor refer to your weakness in the presence of your foes.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The joy of one's foes will be destroyed if one guards oneself by knowing the way (of acting) and securing assistance.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A thorny tree should be felled while young, (for) when it is grown it will destroy the hand of the feller.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who do not destroy the pride of those who hate (them) will certainly not exist even to breathe.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Shade and water are not pleasant, (if) they cause disease; so are the qualities of (one's) relations not agreeable, (if) they cause pain.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Fear not foes (who say they would cut) like a sword; (but) fear the friendship of foes (who seemingly act) like relations.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Fear internal enmity and guard yourself; (if not) it will destroy (you) in an evil hour, as surely as the tool which cuts the potter's clay.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The secret enmity of a person whose mind in unreformed will lead to many evils causing disaffection among (one's) relations.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If there appears internal hatred in a (king's) family; it will lead to many a fatal crime.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If hatred arises among (one's) own people, it will be hardly possible (for one) to escape death.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Never indeed will a family subject to internal hatred unite (really) though it may present an apparent union like that of a casket and its lid.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A family subject to internal hatred will wear out and lose its strength like iron that has been filed away.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although internal hatred be as small as the fragment of the sesamum (seed), still does destruction dwell in it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Living with those who do not agree (with one) is like dwelling with a cobra (in the same) hut.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)
