text: Not to disregard the power of those who can carry out (their wishes) is more important than all the watchfulness of those who guard (themselves against evil).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To behave without respect for the great (rulers) will make them do (us) irremediable evils.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a person desires ruin, let him not listen to the righteous dictates of law, but commit crimes against those who are able to slay (other sovereigns).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The weak doing evil to the strong is like beckoning Yama to come (and destroy them).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who have incurred the wrath of a cruel and mighty potentate will not prosper wherever they may go.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though burnt by a fire (from a forest), one may perhaps live; (but) never will he live who has shown disrespect to the great (devotees).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If a king incurs the wrath of the righteous great, what will become of his government with its splendid auxiliaries and (all) its untold wealth ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If (the) hill-like (devotees) resolve on destruction, those who seemed to be everlasting will be destroyed root and branch from the earth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If those of exalted vows burst in a rage, even (Indra) the king will suffer a sudden loss and be entirely ruined.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though in possession of numerous auxiliaries, they will perish who are-exposed to the wrath of the noble whose penance is boundless.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who lust after their wives will not attain the excellence of virtue; and it is just this that is not desired by those who are bent on acquiring wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth of him who, regardless (of his manliness), devotes himself to his wife's feminine nature will cause great shame (to ali men) and to himself.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The frailty that stoops to a wife will always make (her husband) feel ashamed among the good.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The undertaking of one, who fears his wife and is therefore destitute of (bliss), will never be applauded.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He that fears his wife will always be afraid of doing good deeds (even) to the good.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They that fear the bamboo-like shoulders of their wives will be destitute of manliness though they may flourish like the Gods.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even shame faced womanhood is more to be esteemed than the shameless manhood that performs the behests of a wife.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who yield to the wishes of their wives will neither relieve the wants of (their) friends nor perform virtuous deeds.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: From those who obey the commands of their wives are to be expected neither deeds of virtue, nor those of wealth nor (even) those of pleasure.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The foolishness that results from devotion to a wife will never be found in those who possess a reflecting mind and a prosperity (flowing) therefrom.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The sweet words of elegant braceleted (prostitutes) who desire (a man) not from affection but from avarice, will cause sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: One must ascertain the character of the ill-natured women who after ascertaining the wealth (of a man) speak (as if they were) good natured-ones, and avoid intercourse (with them).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The false embraces of wealth-loving women are like (hired men) embracing a strange corpse in a dark room.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wise who seek the wealth of grace will not desire the base favours of those who regard wealth (and not pleasure) as (their) riches.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those whose knowledge is made excellent by their (natural) sense will not covet the trffling delights of those whose favours are common (to all).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who would spread (the fame of) their own goodness will not desire the shoulders of those who rejoice in their accomplishments and bestow their despicable favours (on all who pay).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who are destitute of a perfectly (reformed) mind will covet the shoulders of those who embrace (them) while their hearts covet other things.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wise say that to such as are destitute of discerning sense the embraces of faithless women are (as ruinous as those of) the celestail female.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The delicate shoulders of prostitutes with excellent jewels are a hell into which are plunged the ignorant base
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Treacherous women, liquor, and gambling are the associates of such as have forsaken by Fortune.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who always thirst after drink will neither inspire fear (in others) nor retain the light (of their fame).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let no liquor be drunk; if it is desired, let it be drunk by those who care not for esteem of the great.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Intoxication is painful even in the presence of (one's) mother; what will it not then be in that of the wise ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The fair maid of modesty will turn her back on those who are guilty of the great and abominable crime of drunkenness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To give money and purchase unconsciousness is the result of one's ignorance of (one's own actions).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They that sleep resemble the deed; (likewise) they that drink are no other than poison-eaters.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who always intoxicate themselves by a private (indulgence in) drink; will have their secrets detected and laughed at by their fellow-townsmen.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let (the drunkard) give up saying "I have never drunk"; (for) the moment (he drinks) he will simply betray his former attempt to conceal.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Reasoning with a drunkard is like going under water with a torch in search of a drowned man.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When (a drunkard) who is sober sees one who is not, it looks as if he remembered not the evil effects of his (own) drink.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though able to win, let not one desire gambling; (for) even what is won is like a fish swallowing the iron in fish-hook.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is there indeed a means of livelihood that can bestow happiness on gamblers who gain one and lose a hundred ?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the king is incessantly addicted to the rolling dice in the hope of gain, his wealth and the resources thereof will take their departure and fall into other's hands.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is nothing else that brings (us) poverty like gambling which causes many a misery and destroys (one's) reputation.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Penniless are those who by reason of their attachment would never forsake gambling, the gambling-place and the handling (of dice).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who are swallowed by the goddess called "gambling" will never have their hunger satisfied, but suffer the pangs of hell in the next world.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To waste time at the place of gambling will destroy inherited wealth and goodness of character.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Gambling destroys property, teaches falsehood, puts an end to benevolence, and brings in misery (here and hereafter).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The habit of gambling prevents the attainment of these five: clothing, wealth, food, fame and learning.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As the gambler loves (his vice) the more he loses by it, so does the soul love (the body) the more it suffers through it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If (food and work are either) excessive or deficient, the three things enumerated by (medical) writers, flatulence, biliousness, and phlegm, will cause (one) disease.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: No medicine is necessary for him who eats after assuring (himself) that what he has (already) eaten has been digested.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If (one's food has been) digested let one eat with moderation; (for) that is the way to prolong the life of an embodied soul.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (First) assure yourself that your food has been digested and never fail to eat, when very hungry, whatever is not disagreeable (to you).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There will be no disaster to one's life if one eats with moderation, food that is not disagreeable.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As pleasure dwells with him who eats moderately, so disease (dwells) with the glutton who eats voraciously.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He will be afflicted with numberless diseases, who eats immoderately, ignorant (of the rules of health).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let the physician enquire into the (nature of the) disease, its cause and its method of cure and treat it faithfully according to (medical rule).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The learned (physician) should ascertain the condition of his patient; the nature of his disease, and the season (of the year) and (then) proceed (with his treatment).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Medical science consists of four parts, viz., patient, physician, medicine and compounder; and each of these (again) contains four sub-divisions.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Consistency (of thought, word and deed) and fear (of sin) are conjointly natural only to the high-born.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The high-born will never deviate from these three; good manners, truthfulness and modestyThe high-born will never deviate from these three; good manners, truthfulness and modesty.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A cheerful countenance, liberality, pleasant words, and an unreviling disposition, these four are said to be the proper qualities of the truly high-born.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though blessed with immense wealth, the noble will never do anything unbecoming.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though their means fall off, those born in ancient families, will not lose their character (for liberality).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who seek to preserve the irreproachable honour of their families will not viciously do what is detrimental thereto.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The defects of the noble will be observed as clearly as the dark spots in the moon.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If one of a good family betrays want of affection, his descent from it will be called in question.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As the sprout indicates the nature of the soil, (so) the speech of the noble indicates (that of one's birth).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who desires a good name must desire modesty; and he who desires (the continuance of) a family greatness must be submissive to all.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Actions that would degrade (one's) family should not be done; though they may be so important that not doing them would end in death.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who desire (to maintain their) honour, will surely do nothing dishonourable, even for the sake of fame.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In great prosperity humility is becoming; dignity, in great adversity.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They who have fallen from their (high) position are like the hair which has fallen from the head.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even those who are exalted like a hill will be thought low, if they commit deeds that are debasing.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Of what good is it (for the high-born) to go and stand in vain before those who revile him ? it only brings him loss of honour and exclusion from heaven.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is better for a man to be said of him that he died in his usual state than that he eked out his life by following those who disgraced him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: For the high-born to keep their body in life when their honour is gone will certainly not prove a remedy against death.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who give up (their) life when (their) honour is at stake are like the yark which kills itself at the loss of (even one of) its hairs.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The world will (always) praise and adore the fame of the honourable who would rather die than suffer indignity.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: One's light is the abundance of one's courage; one's darkness is the desire to live destitute of such (a state of mind).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: All human beings agree as regards their birth but differ as regards their characteristics, because of the different qualities of their actions.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though (raised) above, the base cannot become great; though (brought) low, the great cannot become base.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even greatness, like a woman's chastity, belongs only to him who guards himself.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (Though reduced) the great will be able to perform, in the proper way, deeds difficult (for others to do).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is never in the nature of the base to seek the society of the great and partake of their nature.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even nobility of birth, wealth and learning, if in (the possession of) the base, will (only) produce everincreasing pride.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The great will always humble himself; but the mean will exalt himself in self-admiration.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Freedom from conceit is (the nature of true) greatness; (while) obstinacy therein is (that of) meanness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The great hide the faults of others; the base only divulge them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is said that those who are conscious of their duty and behave with a perfect goodness will regard as natural all that is good.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The only delight of the perfect is that of their goodness; all other (sensual) delights are not to be included among any (true) delights.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Affection, fear (of sin), benevolence, favour and truthfulness; these are the five pillars on which perfect goodness rests.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Penance consists in the goodness that kills not , and perfection in the goodness that tells not others' faults.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Stooping (to inferiors) is the strength of those who can accomplish (an undertaking); and that is the weapon with which the great avert their foes.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The touch-stone of perfection is to receive a defeat even at the hands of one's inferiors.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Of what avail is perfect goodness if it cannot do pleasing things even to those who have pained (it) ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)
locator: data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet row 986, column couplet [repaired: printed page leaf 477, share 1.0]

text: Poverty is no disgrace to one who abounds in good qualities.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who are said to be the shore of the sea of perfection will never change, though ages may change.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If there is a defect in the character of the perfect, (even) the great world cannot bear (its) burden.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If one is easy of access to all, it will be easy for one to obtain the virtue called goodness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Affectionateness and birth in a good family, these two constitute what is called a proper behaviour to all.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Resemblance of bodies is no resemblance of souls; true resemblance is the resemblance of qualities that attract.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The world applauds the character of those whose usefulness results from their equity and charity.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Reproach is painful to one even in sport; those (therefore) who know the nature of others exhibit (pleasing) qualities even when they are hated.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The (way of the) world subsists by contact with the good; if not, it would bury itself in the earth and perish.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who is destitute of (true) human qualities (only) resembles a tree, though he may possess the sharpness of a file.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is wrong (for the wise) not to exhibit (good) qualities even towards those who bearing no friendship (for them) do only what is hateful.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To those who cannot rejoice, the wide world is buried darkness even in (broad) day light.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The great wealth obtained by one who has no goodness will perish like pure milk spoilt by the impurity of the vessel.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who does not enjoy the immense riches he has heaped up in his house, is (to be reckoned as) dead, (for) there is nothing achieved (by him).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who knows that wealth yields every pleasure and yet is so blind as to lead miserly life will be born a demon.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A burden to the earth are men bent on the acquisition of riches and not (true) fame.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What will the miser who is not liked (by any one) regard as his own (in the world to come) ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who neither give (to others) nor enjoy (their property) are (truly) destitute, though possessing immense riches.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who enjoys not (his riches) nor relieves the wants of the worthy is a disease to his wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth of him who never bestows anything on the destitute is like a woman of beauty growing old without a husband.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The wealth of him who is disliked (by all) is like the fruit-bearing of the etty tree in the midst of a town.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Strangers will inherit the riches that have been acquired without regard for friendship, comfort and charity.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The short-lived poverty of those who are noble and rich is like the clouds becoming poor (for a while).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: True modesty is the fear of (evil) deeds; all other modesty is (simply) the bashfulness of virtuous maids.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Food, clothing and the like are common to all men but modesty is peculiar to the good.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As the body is the abode of the spirit, so the excellence of modesty is the abode of perfection.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The Is not the modesty ornament of the noble ? Without it, their haughtiness would be a pain (to others).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The world regards as the abode of modesty him who fear his own and other's guilt.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The great make modesty their barrier (of defence) and not the wide world.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The modest would rather lose their life for the sake of modesty than lose modesty for the sake of life.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Virtue is likely to forsake him who shamelessly does what others are ashamed of.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Want of manners injures one's family; but want of modesty injures one's character.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The actions of those who are without modesty at heart are like those of puppet moved by a string.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is no higher greatness than that of one saying. I will not cease in my effort (to raise my family).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: One's family is raised by untiring perseverance in both effort and wise contrivances.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The Deity will clothe itself and appear before him who resolves on raising his family.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those who are prompt in their efforts (to better their family) need no deliberation, such efforts will of themselves succeed.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: People will eagerly seek the friendship of the prosperous soul who has raised his family without foul means.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A man's true manliness consists in making himself the head and benefactor of his family.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Like heroes in the battle-field, the burden (of protection etc.) is borne by those who are the most efficient in a family.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As a family suffers by (one's) indolence and false dignity there is to be so season (good or bad) to those who strive to raise their family.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is it only to suffering that his body is exposed who undertakes to preserve his family from evil ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If there are none to prop up and maintain a family (in distress), it will fall at the stroke of the axe of misfortune.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Agriculture, though laborious, is the most excellent (form of labour); for people, though they go about (in search of various employments), have at last to resort to the farmer.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Agriculturists are (as it were) the linch-pin of the world for they support all other workers who cannot till the soil.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They alone live who live by agriculture; all others lead a cringing, dependent life.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The Patriotic farmers desire to bring all other states under the control of their own king.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those whose nature is to live by manual labour will never beg but give something to those who beg.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the farmer's hands are slackened, even the ascetic state will fail.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the land is dried so as to reduce one ounce of earth to a quarter, it will grow plentifully even without a handful of manure.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Manuring is better than ploughing; after weeding, watching is better than watering (it).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the owner does not (personally) attend to his cultivation, his land will behave like an angry wife and yield him no pleasure.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The maiden, Earth, will laugh at the sight of those who plead poverty and lead an idle life.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is nothing that afflicts (one) like poverty.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When cruel poverty comes on, it deprives one of both the present and future (bliss).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Hankering poverty destroys at once the greatness of (one's) ancient descent and (the dignity of one's) speech.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even in those of high birth, poverty will produce the fault of uttering mean words.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The misery of poverty brings in its train many (more) miseries.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The words of the poor are profitless, though they may be sound in thought and clear in expression.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He that is reduced to absolute poverty will be regarded as a stranger even by his own mother.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is the poverty that almost killed me yesterday, to meet me today too ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: One may sleep in the midst of fire; but by no means in the midst of poverty.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The destitute poor, who do not renounce their bodies, only consume their neighbour's salt and water.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If you meet with those that may be begged of, you may beg; (but) if they withhold (their gift) it is their blame and not yours.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even begging may be pleasant, if what is begged for is obtained without grief (to him that begs).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is even a beauty in standing before and begging of those who are liberal in their gifts and understand their duty (to beggars).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To beg of such as never think of withholding (their charity) even in their dreams, is in fact the same as giving (it oneself).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As there are in the world those that give without refusing, there are (also) those that prefer to beg by simply standing before them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: All the evil of begging will be removed at the sight of those who are far from the evil of refusing.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Beggars rejoice exceedingly when they behold those who bestow (their alms) with kindness and courtesy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If there were no beggars, (the actions done in) the cool wide world would only resemble the movement of a puppet.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What (praise) would there be to givers (of alms) if there were no beggars to ask for and reveive (them).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who begs ought not to be angry (at a refusal); for even the misery of (his own) poverty should be a sufficient reason (for so doing).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not to beg (at all) even from those excellent persons who cheerfully give without refusing, will do immense good.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the Creator of the world has decreed even begging as a means of livelihood, may he too go abegging and perish.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is no greater folly than the boldness with which one seeks to remedy the evils of poverty by begging (rather than by working).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even the whole world cannot sufficiently praise the dignity that would not beg even in the midst of destitution.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even thin gruel is ambrosia to him who has obtained it by labour.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is nothing more disgraceful to one's tongue than to use it in begging water even for a cow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I beseech all beggars and say, "If you need to beg, never beg of those who give unwillingly".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The unsafe raft of begging will split when it strikes on the rock of refusal.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To think of (the evil of) begging is enough to melt one's heart; but to think of refusal is enough to break it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Saying "No" to a beggar takes away his life. (but as that very word will kill the refuser) where then would the latter's life hide itself ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The base resemble men perfectly (as regards form); and we have not seen such (exact) resemblance (among any other species).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The low enjoy more felicity than those who know what is good; for the former are not troubled with anxiety (as to the good).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The base resemble the Gods; for the base act as they like.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The base feels proud when he sees persons whose acts meaner than his own.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (The principle of) behaviour in the mean is chiefly fear; if not, hope of gain, to some extent.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The base are like a drum that is beaten, for they unburden to others the secrets they have heard
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The mean will not (even) shake off (what sticks to) their hands (soon after a meal) to any but those who would break their jaws with their clenched fists.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The great bestow (their alms) as soon as they are informed; (but) the mean, like the sugar-cane, only when they are tortured to death.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The base will bring an evil (accusation) against others, as soon as he sees them (enjoying) good food and clothing.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The base will hasten to sell themselves as soon as a calamity has befallen them. For what else are they fitted ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is this jewelled female a celestial, a choice peahen, or a human being ? My mind is perplexed
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: This female beauty returning my looks is like a celestial maiden coming with an army to contend against me.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I never knew before what is called Yama; I see it now; it is the eyes that carry on a great fight with (the help of) female qualities.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: These eyes that seem to kill those who look at them are as it were in hostilities with this feminine simplicity.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is it Yama, (a pair of) eyes or a hind ?- Are not all these three in the looks of this maid ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Her eyes will cause (me) no trembling sorrow, if they are properly hidden by her cruel arched eye-brows.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The cloth that covers the firm bosom of this maiden is (like) that which covers the eyes of a rutting elephant.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: On her bright brow alone is destroyed even that power of mine that used to terrify the most fearless foes in the battlefield.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Of what use are other jewels to her who is adorned with modesty, and the meek looks of a hind ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Unlike boiled honey which yields delight only when it is drunk, love gives pleasure even when looked at.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There are two looks in the dyed eyes of this (fair one); one causes pain, and the other is the cure thereof.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A single stolen glance of her eyes is more than half the pleasure (of sexual embrace).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: She has looked (at men) and stooped (her head); and that (sign) waters as it were (the corn of) our love.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I look, she looks down; when I do not, she looks and smiles gently.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: She not only avoids a direct look at me, but looks as it were with a half-closed eye and smiles.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though they may speak harshly as if they were strangers, the words of the friendly are soon understood.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Little words that are harsh and looks that are hateful are (but) the expressions of lovers who wish to act like strangers.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I look, the pitying maid looks in return and smiles gently; and that is a comforting sign for me.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Both the lovers are capable of looking at each other in an ordinary way, as if they were perfect strangers.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The words of the mouths are of no use whatever, when there is perfect agreement between the eyes (of lovers).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The (simultaneous) enjoyment of the five senses of sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch can only be found with bright braceleted (women).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The remedy for a disease is always something different (from it); but for the disease caused by this jewelled maid, she is herself the cure.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Can the lotus-eyed Vishnu's heaven be indeed as sweet to those who delight to sleep in the delicate arms of their beloved ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: From whence has she got this fire that burns when I withdraw and cools when I approach ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The shoulders of her whose locks are adorned with flowers delight me as if they were the very sweets I have desired (to get).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The shoulders of this fair one are made of ambrosia, for they revive me with pleasure every time I embrace them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The embraces of a gold-complexioned beautiful female are as pleasant as to dwell in one's own house and live by one's own (earnings) after distributing (a portion of it in charity).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To ardent lovers sweet is the embrace that cannot be penetrated even by a breath of breeze.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Love quarrel, reconciliation and intercourse - these are the advantages reaped by those who marry for lust.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As (one's) ignorance is discovered the more one learns, so does repeated intercourse with a well-adorned female (only create a desire for more).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: May you flourish, O Anicham! you have a delicate nature. But my beloved is more delicate than you.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my soul, fancying that flowers which are seen by many can resemble her eyes, you become confused at the sight of them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The complexion of this bamboo-shouldered one is that of a shoot; her teeth, are pearls; her breath, fragrance; and her dyed eyes, lances.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If the blue lotus could see, it would stoop and look at the ground saying, "I can never resemble the eyes of this excellent jewelled one".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: No merry drums will be beaten for the (tender) waist of her who has adorned herself with the anicham without having removed its stem.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The stars have become confused in their places not being able to distinguish between the moon and the maid's countenance.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Could there be spots in the face of this maid like those in the bright full moon ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If you can indeed shine like the face of women, flourish, O moon, for then would you be worth loving ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O moon, if you wish to resemble the face of her whose eyes are like (these) flowers, do not appear so as to be seen by all.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The anicham and the feathers of the swan are to the feet of females, like the fruit of the (thorny) Nerunji.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The water which oozes from the white teeth of this soft speeched damsel is like a mixture of milk and honey.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The love between me and this damsel is like the union of body and soul.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O you image in the pupil (of my eye)! depart; there is no room for (my) fair-browed beloved.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My fair-jewelled one resembles the living soul (when she is in union with me), the dying soul when she leaves me.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If I had forgotten her who has bright battling eyes, I would have remembered (thee); but I never forget her. (Thus says he to her maid).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My lover would not depart from mine eyes; even if I wink, he would not suffer (from pain); he is so ethereal.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As my lover abides in my eyes, I will not even paint them, for he would (then) have to conceal himself.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As my lover is in my heart, I am afraid of eating (anything) hot, for I know it would pain him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I will not wink, knowing that if I did, my lover would hide himself; and for this reason, this town says, he is unloving.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My lover dwells in my heart with perpetual delight; but the town says he is unloving and (therefore) dwells afar.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To those who after enjoyment of sexual pleasure suffer (for want of more), there is no help so efficient as the palmyra horse.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Having got rid of shame, the suffering body and soul save themselves on the palmyra horse.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Modesty and manliness were once my own; now, my own is the palmyra horse that is ridden by the lustful.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The raft of modesty and manliness, is, alas, carried-off by the strong current of lust.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: She with the small garland-like bracelets has given me the palmyra horse and the sorrow that is endured at night.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Mine eyes will not close in sleep on your mistress's account; even at midnight will I think of mounting the palmyra horse.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is nothing so noble as the womanly nature that would not ride the palmyra horse, though plunged a sea of lust.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even the Lust (of women) transgresses its secrecy and appears in public, forgetting that they are too chaste and liberal (to be overcome by it).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My lust, feeling that it is not known by all, reels confused in the streets (of this town).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even strangers laugh (at us) so as to be seen by us, for they have not suffered.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My precious life is saved by the raise of rumour, and this, to my good luck no others are aware of.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not knowing the value of her whose eyes are like flowers this town has got up a rumour about me.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Will I not get a rumour that is known to the (whole) town ? For what I have not got is as if I had got it (already).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Rumour increases the violence of my passion; without it it would grow weak and waste away.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As drinking liquor is delightful (to one) whenever one is in mirth, so is lust delightful to me whenever it is the subject of rumour.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It was but a single day that I looked on (my lover); but the rumour thereof has spread like the seizure of the moon by the serpent.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: This malady (of lust) is manured by the talk of women and watered by the (harsh) words of my mother.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To say that one could extinguish passion by rumour is like extinguishing fire with ghee.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When the departure of him who said "fear not" has put me to shame before others, why need I be ashamed of scandal.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The rumour I desire is raised by the town (itself); and my lover would if desired consent (to my following him).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If it is not departure, tell me; but if it is your speedy return, tell it to those who would be alive then.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: His very look was once pleasing; but (now) even intercourse is painful through fear of separation.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As even the lover who understands (everything) may at times depart, confidence is hardly possible.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If he who bestowed his love and said "fear not" should depart, will it be the fault of those who believed in (his) assuring words ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If you would save (my life), delay the departure of my destined (husband); for if he departs, intercourse will become impossible.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If he is so cruel as to mention his departure (to me), the hope that he would bestow (his love) must be given up.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Do not the rings that begin to slide down my fingers forebode the separation of my lord ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Painful is it to live in a friendless town; but far more painful is it to part from one's lover.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Fire burns when touched; but, like the sickness of love, can it also burn when removed ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As if there were many indeed that can consent to the impossible, kill their pain, endure separation and yet continue to live afterwards.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I would hide this pain from others; but it (only) swells like a spring to those who drain it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I cannot conceal this pain, nor can I relate it without shame to him who has caused it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: (Both) lust and shame, with my soul for their shoulder pole balance themselves on a body that cannot bear them.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is indeed a flood of lust; but there is no raft of safety to cross it with.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who can produce sorrow from friendship, what can he not bring forth out of enmity ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The pleasure of lust is (as great as) the sea; but the pain of lust is far greater.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I have swam across the terrible flood of lust, but have not seen its shore; even at midnight I am alone; still I live.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The night which graciously lulls to sleep all living creatures, has me alone for her companion.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The long nights of these days are far more cruel than the heartless one who is torturing me.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Could mine eyes travel like my thoughts to the abode (of my absent lord), they would not swim in this flood of tears.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: As this incurable malady has been caused by my eyes which showed (him) to me, why should they now weep for (him).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The dyed eyes that (then) looked without foresight, why should they now endure sorrow, without feeling sharply (their own fault).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They themselves looked eagerly (on him) and now they weep. Is not this to be laughed at ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: These painted eyes have caused me a lasting mortal disease; and now they can weep no more, the tears having dried up.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Mine eyes have caused me a lust that is greater than the sea and (they themselves) endure the torture of sleeplessness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The eyes that have given me this disease have themselves been seized with this (suffering). Oh! I am much delighted.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The eyes that became tender and gazed intently on him, may they suffer so much as to dry up the fountain of their tears.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He is indeed here who loved me with his lips but not with his heart but mine eyes suffer from not seeing him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When he is away they do not sleep; when he is present they do not sleep; in either case, mine eyes endure unbearable agony.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is not difficult for the people of this place to understand the secret of those whose eyes, like mine, are as it were beaten drums.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I who (then) consented to the absence of my loving lord, to whom can I (now) relate the fact of my having turned sallow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sallowness, as if proud of having been caused by him, would now ride on my person.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He has taken (away) my beauty and modesty, and given me instead disease and sallowness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I think (of him); and what I speak about is but his excellence; still is there sallowness; and this is deceitful.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Just as my lover departed then, did not sallowness spread here on my person ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Just as darkness waits for the failing light; so does sallowness wait for the laxity of my husband's intercourse.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I who was in close embrace just turned aside and the moment I did so, sallowness came on me like something to be seized on.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Besides those who say "she has turned sallow" there are none who say "he has forsaken her".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If he is clear of guilt who has conciliated me (to his departure) let my body suffer its due and turn sallow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It would be good to be said of me that I have turned sallow, if friends do not reproach with unkindness him who pleased me (then).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The women who are beloved by those whom they love, have they have not got the stone-less fruit of sexual delight ?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The bestowal of love by the beloved on those who love them is like the rain raining (at the proper season) on those who live by it.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The pride that says "we shall live" suits only those who are loved by their beloved (husbands).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even those who are esteemed (by other women) are devoid of excellence, if they are not loved by their beloved.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who is beloved by me, what will he do to me, if I am not beloved by him ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Lust, like the weight of the KAVADI, pains if it lies in one end only but pleases if it is in both.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Would not cupid who abides and contends in one party (only) witness the pain and sorrow (in that party)?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)
