text: There is no one in the world so hard-hearted as those who can live without receiving (even) a kind word from their beloved.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though my beloved bestows no love on one, still are his words sweet to my ears.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Live, O my soul, would you who relate your great sorrow to strangers, try rather to fill up your own sea (of sorrow).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sexuality is sweeter than liquor, because when remembered, it creates a most rapturous delight
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even to think of one's beloved gives one no pain. Sexuality, in any degree, is always delightful.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I feel as if I am going to sneeze but do not, and (therefore) my beloved is about to think (of me) but does not.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He continues to abide in my soul, do I likewise abide in his ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He who has imprisoned me in his soul, is he ashamed to enter incessantly into mine.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I live by remembering my (former) intercourse with him; if it were not so, how could I live ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I have never forgotten (the pleasure); even to think of it burns my soul; could I live, if I should ever forget it ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: He will not be angry however much I may think of him; is it not so much the delight my beloved affords me ? .
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My precious life is wasting away by thinking too much on the cruelty of him who said we were not different.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: May you live, O Moon! Do not set, that I mine see him who has departed without quitting my soul.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Where with shall I feast the dream which has brought me my dear one's messenger ?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If my fish-like painted eyes should, at my begging, close in sleep, I could fully relate my sufferings to my lord.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My life lasts because in my dream I behold him who does not favour me in my waking hours.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is pleasure in my dream, because in it I seek and obtain him who does not visit me in my wakefulness.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I saw him in my waking hours, and then it was pleasant; I see him just now in my dream, and it is (equally) pleasant.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Were there no such thing as wakefulness, my beloved (who visited me) in my dream would not depart from me.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The cruel one who would not favour me in my wakefulness, what right has he to torture me in my dreams?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I am asleep he rests on my shoulders, (but) when I awake he hastens into my soul.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: They who have no dear ones to behold in their dreams blame him who visits me not in my waking hours.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The women of this place say he has forsaken me in my wakefulness. I think they have not seen him visit me in my dreams.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Live, O you evening are you (the former) evening? No, you are the season that slays (married) women
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A long life to you, O dark evening! You are sightless. Is your help-mate (also) as hard-hearted as mine.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The evening that (once) came in with trembling and dimness (now) brings me an aversion for life and increasing sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In the absence of my lover, evening comes in like slayers on the field of slaughter.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What good have I done to morning (and) what evil to evening?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Previous to my husband's departure, I know not the painful nature of evening.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: This malady buds forth in the morning, expands all day long and blossoms in the evening.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The shepherd's flute now sounds as a fiery forerunner of night, and is become a weapon that slays (me).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When night comes on confusing (everyone's) mind, the (whole) town will lose its sense and be plunged in sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My (hitherto) unextinguished life is now lost in this bewildering night at the thought of him who has the nature of wealth.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: While we endure the unbearable sorrow, your eyes weep for him who is gone afar, and shun (the sight of) fragrant flowers.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The discoloured eyes that shed tears profusely seem to betray the unkindness of our beloved.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The shoulders that swelled on the day of our union (now) seem to announce our separation clearly (to the public).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In the absence of your consort, your shoulders having lost their former beauty and fulness, your bracelets of pure gold have become loose.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The (loosened) bracelets, and the shoulders from which the old beauty has faded, relate the cruelty of the pitiless one.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I am greatly pained to hear you call him a cruel man, just because your shoulders are reduced and your bracelets loosened.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Can you O my soul! gain glory by relating to the (so-called) cruel one the clamour of my fading shoulders?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I once loosened the arms that were in embrace, the forehead of the gold-braceleted women turned sallow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When but a breath of breeze penetrated our embrace, her large cool eyes became sallow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Was it at the sight of what the bright forehead had done that the sallowness of her eyes became sad?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my soul, will you not think and tell me some medicine be it what it may, that can cure this incurable malady?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: May you live, O my soul! While he is without love, for you to suffer is (simple) folly.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my soul! why remain (here) and suffer thinking (of him)? There are no lewd thoughts (of you) in him who has caused you this disease of sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my soul! take my eyes also with you, (if not), these would eat me up (in their desire) to see him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my soul! can he who loves not though he is beloved, be forsaken saying he hates me (now)?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my soul! when you see the dear one who remove dislike by intercourse, you are displeased and continue to be so. Nay, your displeasure is (simply) false.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my good soul, give up either lust or honour, as for me I can endure neither.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: You are a fool, O my soul! to go after my departed one, while you mourn that he is not kind enough to favour you.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my soul! to whom would you repair, while the dear one is within yourself?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If I retain in my heart him who has left me without befriending me, I shall lose even the (inward) beauty that remains.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The axe of lust can break the door of chastity which is bolted with the bolt of modesty.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)
locator: data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet row 1250, column couplet [repaired: printed page leaf 603, share 1.0]

text: Even at midnight is my mind worried by lust, and this one thing, alas! is without mercy.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I would conceal my lust, but alas, it yields not to my will but breaks out like a sneeze.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I say I would be firm, but alas, my malady breaks out from its concealment and appears in public.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The dignity that would not go after an absent lover is not known to those who are sticken by love.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The sorrow I have endured by desiring to go after my absent lover, in what way is it excellent?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I know nothing like shame when my beloved does from love (just) what is desired (by me).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Are not the enticing words of my trick-abounding roguish lover the weapon that breaks away my feminine firmness?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I said I would feign dislike and so went (away); (but) I embraced him the moment I say my mind began to unite with him!.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is it possible for those whose hearts melt like fat in the fire to say they can feign a strong dislike and remain so?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My finger has worn away by marking (on the wall) the days he has been absent while my eyes have lost their lustre and begin to fail.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O you bright-jewelled maid, if I forget (him) today, my shoulders will lose their beauty even in the other life and make my bracelets loose.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: still live by longing for the arrival of him who has gone out of love for victory and with valour as his guide.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My heart is rid of its sorrow and swells with rapture to think of my absent lover returning with his love.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: May I look on my lover till I am satisfied and thereafter will vanish the sallowness of my slender shoulders.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: May my husband return some day; and then will I enjoy (him) so as to destroy all this agonizing sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: On the return of him who is as dear as my eyes, am I displeased or am I to embrace (him); or am I to do both?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)
locator: data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet row 1266, column couplet [repaired: printed page leaf 611, share 0.87]

text: Let the king fight and gain (victories); (but) let me be united to my wife and feast the evening.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To those who suffer waiting for the day of return of their distant lovers one day is as long as seven days.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: After (my wife) has died of a broken heart, what good will there be if she is to receive me, has received me, or has even embraced me?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though you would conceal (your feelings), your painted eyes would not, for, transgressing (their bounds), they tell (me) something.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Unusually great is the female simplicity of your maid whose beauty fills my eyes and whose shoulders resemble the bamboo.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is something that is implied in the beauty of this woman, like the thread that is visible in a garland of gems.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: There is something in the unmatured smile of this maid like the fragrance that is contained in an unblossomed bud.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The well-meant departure of her whose bangles are tight-fitting contains a remedy that can cure my great sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The embrace that fills me with comfort and gladness is capable of enduring (my former) sorrow and meditating on his want of love.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My bracelets have understood before me the (mental) separation of him who rules the cool seashore.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It was but yesterday my lover departed (from me); and it is seven days since my complexion turned sallow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: She looked at her bracelets, her tender shoulders, and her feet; this was what she did there (significantly).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To express their love-sickness by their eyes and resort to begging bespeaks more than ordinary female excellence.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To please by thought and cheer by sight is peculiar, not to liquor but lust.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: If women have a lust that exceeds even the measure of the palmyra fruit, they will not desire (to feign) dislike even as much as the millet.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though my eyes disregard me and do what is pleasing to my husband, still will they not be satisfied unless they see him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my friend! I was prepared to feign displeasure but my mind forgetting it was ready to embrace him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Like the eyes which see not the pencil that paints it, I cannot see my husband's fault (just) when I meet him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I see my husband, I do not see any faults; but when I do not see him, I do not see anything but faults.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Like those who leap into a stream which they know will carry them off, why should a wife feign dislike which she knows cannot hold out long?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O you rogue! your breast is to me what liquor is to those who rejoice in it, though it only gives them an unpleasant disgrace.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sexual delight is more delicate than a flower, and few are those who understand its real nature.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: She once feigned dislike in her eyes, but the warmth of her embrace exceeded my own.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my soul! although you have seen how his soul stands by him, how is it you do not stand by me?
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: my soul! although you have known him who does not love me, still do you go to him, saying "he will not be displeased.".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my soul! do you follow him at pleasure under the belief that the ruined have no friends?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: O my soul! you would not first seem sulky and then enjoy (him); who then would in future consult you about such things?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My soul fears when it is without him; it also fears when it is with him; it is subject to incessant sorrow.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My mind has been (here) in order to eat me up (as it were) whenever I think of him in my solitude.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: I have even forgotten my modesty, having been caught in my foolish mind which is not dignified enough to forget him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: My soul which clings to life thinks only of his (own) gain in the belief that it would be disgraceful for it to despise him.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Who would help me out of one's distress, when one's own soul refuses help to one? .
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is hardly possible for strangers to behave like relations, when one's own soul acts like a stranger.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Let us witness awhile his keen suffering; just feign dislike and embrace him not.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: A little dislike is like salt in proportion; to prolong it a little is like salt a little too much.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: For men not to embrace those who have feigned dislike is like torturing those already in agony.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Not to reconcile those who have feigned dislike is like cutting a faded creeper at its root.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: An increased shyness in those whose eyes are like flowers is beautiful even to good and virtuous husbands.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Sexual pleasure, without prolonged and short-lived dislike, is like too ripe, and unripe fruit.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: The doubt as to whether intercourse would take place soon or not, creates a sorrow (even) in feigned dislike.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: What avails sorrow when I am without a wife who can understand the cause of my sorrow?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Like water in the shade, dislike is delicious only in those who love.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: It is nothing but strong desire that makes her mind unite with me who can leave her to her own dislike.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: You are given to prostitution; all those who are born as womankind enjoy you with their eyes in an ordinary way. I will not embrace you.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I continued to be sulky he sneezed and thought I would (then) wish him a long life.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even if I were adorned with a garland of branch-flowers, she would say I did so to show it to another woman.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I said I loved her more than any other woman, she said "more than others, yes, more than others," and remained sulky.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I said I would never part from her in this life her eyes were filled with tears.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I said I had remembered her, she said I had forgotten her and relaxing her embrace, began to feign dislike.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I sneezed she blessed me, but at once changed (her mind) and wept, asking, "At the thought of whom did you sneeze?".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: When I suppressed my sneezing, she wept saying, "I suppose you (did so) to hide from me your own people's remembrance of you".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even when I try to remove her dislike, she is displeased and says, "This is the way you behave towards (other women)."
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Even when I look on her contemplating (her beauty), she is displeased and says, "With whose thought have you (thus) looked on my person?".
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Although my husband is free from defects, the way in which he embraces me is such as to make me feign dislike.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: His love will increase though it may (at first seem to) fade through the short-lived distress caused by (my) dislike.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Is there a celestial land that can please like the feigned dislike of those whose union resembles that of earth and water?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: In prolonged dislike after an embrace there is a weapon that can break my heart.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Though free from defects, men feel pleased when they cannot embrace the delicate shoulders of those whom they love.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: To digest what has been eaten is more delightful than to eat more; likewise love is more delightful in dislike than intercourse.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Those are conquerors whose dislike has been defeated and that is proved by the love (which follows).
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Will I enjoy once more through her dislike, the pleasure of that love that makes her forehead perspire?.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: May the bright-jewelled one feign dislike, and may the night be prolonged for me to implore her!.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)

text: Dislike adds delight to love; and a hearty embrace (thereafter) will add delight to dislike.
author: W. H. Drew (kurals 1-630); John Lazarus (631-1330)
work_title: The Cural of Tiruvalluvar (Drew 1840/1852; completed by Lazarus 1885)
